## What has been tested
48. Fat metabolism: Tesamorelin, HIV visceral fat, phase 3 (human)
49. Endocrine & growth: CJC-1295 DAC, GH and IGF-1 rise (human)
50. Endocrine & growth: GHRH + GHRP synergy, normal men (human)
51. Endocrine & growth: Ipamorelin GH release, rats and pigs (animal)
52. Never tested as a combination, and no published protocol for it was found. Tesamorelin alone cut visceral fat about 20% in 26-week HIV trials; CJC-1295 (DAC form) raised GH and IGF-1 in healthy adults; ipamorelin released GH selectively in animals. Two GHRH analogues act on the same receptor, so their effects are not expected to multiply the way GHRH plus GHRP does.
53. What it helps: No data on the triple. The evidence that exists belongs to its parts: tesamorelin's visceral-fat trials, the CJC-1295 DAC GH and IGF-1 study, ipamorelin animal selectivity, and the 1990 human synergy study. Expect the pattern of a GHRH + GHRP blend, with unknown added benefit from the second GHRH analogue.

## Who shouldn't take it
54. Pituitary tumour, pituitary surgery or brain radiation: Label contraindication: needs an intact hypothalamic-pituitary axis. (verified)
55. People with active or recent cancer: Raises GH and IGF-1, which promote cell growth. (inferred)
56. People with prediabetes or poorly controlled diabetes: GH raises blood glucose and insulin resistance. (inferred)
57. Drug-tested athletes: GH secretagogues are banned under WADA S2. (verified)

## Synergies (paired with)
58. Sermorelin: Sermorelin is another GHRH copy acting on the same receptor as tesamorelin and Mod GRF 1-29. Adding it makes a third GHRH source with more overlap, not synergy. The combination has not been tested.
59. MK-677: MK-677 is an oral ghrelin mimic that raises GH all day, on the same receptor as ipamorelin. Stacking it adds a steady background to the pulses. It raises hunger, and the pairing has not been tested together.
60. BPC-157: BPC-157 works on blood vessel growth and makes tendon cells more responsive to growth hormone in rats. People pair it with a GH blend for injury recovery. The pairing is user logic, not trial data.

## Where it comes from
61. A three-part growth hormone blend: two GHRH analogues (tesamorelin and CJC-1295 no DAC, i.e. Mod GRF 1-29) plus the ghrelin-receptor agonist ipamorelin. Sold as 6 + 3 + 3 mg, 12 mg per vial.
62. First studied for: A seller-led extension of CJC/Ipa: tesamorelin is added for its belly-fat trial record, while keeping the cheaper Mod GRF.
63. 1990: GHRP plus GHRH synergy shown in normal men
64. 2006: CJC-1295 (DAC) raises GH and IGF-1 in healthy adults
65. 2007: Tesamorelin cuts visceral fat ~20% in HIV trial
66. 2010: Tesamorelin approved (Egrifta)
67. 2024: PCAC votes against ipamorelin and CJC-1295
68. Today: Sold as a 6/3/3 mg seller blend

# VK2735
Page: https://baresignals.co/library/#/p/vk2735
Checked against Library v68, exported 2026-10-25

## Identity
1. Also called: VK-2735, Viking GLP-1/GIP dual agonist
2. Origin: Lab-designed
3. Legal and approval status: Investigational, not approved anywhere: injectable Phase 3 VANQUISH-1 and -2 fully enrolled (Nov 2025, Mar 2026), 78-week readouts not before late 2027 (reported); oral Phase 3 to start Q4 2026. As an unapproved drug it falls under WADA S0 (inferred).

## Summary
4. VK2735 is Viking Therapeutics' dual GLP-1 and GIP agonist, the same receptor pair as tirzepatide, developed as both a weekly injection and a daily pill. It is aimed at obesity and blood sugar control. In 13-week Phase 2 trials, injections gave up to 14.7% weight loss and the tablet up to 12.2%. Dropouts at the top tablet dose were high, and no community use is documented.
5. Punch line: Viking's tirzepatide-style GLP-1 and GIP dual, weekly shot or daily pill. Up to 14.7% lost in 13 weeks.
6. Used for: Obesity, type 2 diabetes

## Roles (what it is used for, strongest first)
7. Appetite & satiety: Strong hunger suppression
8. Fat metabolism: Up to 14.7% loss in 13 weeks
9. Glucose & insulin: Prediabetes back to normal
10. Heart & vessels: Lower blood pressure in trials

## How it works
11. Quiets hunger in the brain · GLP-1 receptor, hypothalamus · role Appetite & satiety
   VK2735 activates GLP-1 receptors in the hypothalamus and brainstem, the hunger and fullness centres. People feel less hungry and eat less. In 13-week human trials this produced weight loss with no plateau yet.
12. Boosts insulin when glucose is high · GLP-1R and GIPR, beta cells · role Glucose & insulin
   On pancreatic beta cells it activates both GLP-1 and GIP receptors, raising insulin only when glucose is high. In the VENTURE human trial, most people with prediabetes returned to normal glucose. The glucose dependence keeps lows uncommon.
13. GIP arm adds fat-tissue effects and may ease nausea · GIP receptor, adipose · role Fat metabolism
   GIP receptors in fat tissue and the brain are thought to add to weight loss and may soften GLP-1 nausea. This is the same logic as tirzepatide. GI side effects were still common in the trials, so any nausea benefit is unproven here.
14. Slows stomach emptying · GLP-1 receptor, gut · role Appetite & satiety
   GLP-1 receptors along the gut and its nerves slow how fast the stomach empties. Food stays longer, which adds to fullness and blunts sugar spikes after meals. It also accounts for much of the GI discomfort reported.
15. Lowers blood pressure with weight loss · Systemic, secondary · role Heart & vessels
   Blood pressure fell in the VENTURE human trial alongside weight loss. This is a secondary, systemic effect rather than a direct action on blood vessels. It is a measured trial finding, not a proven reduction in heart events.
16. Mechanism overview: VK2735 is a dual agonist of the GLP-1 and GIP receptors, the incretin pair also hit by tirzepatide. GLP-1 receptor activation in the hypothalamus and brainstem cuts hunger and slows stomach emptying, while GLP-1R and GIPR on pancreatic beta cells raise insulin only when glucose is high. GIP receptor signalling in fat tissue and the brain is thought to add to weight loss and may soften GLP-1 nausea. A long half-life of about a week supports weekly injection, and the same molecule is given as a tablet at roughly ten times the injected dose, implying low oral absorption.

17. Typical: 2.5–17.5 mg weekly (inj); 30–120 mg daily (tablet) · weekly (Sub-Q) or daily (oral) · cycle Ongoing (Phase 3: 78 weeks) · route Sub-Q or oral tablet (verified)
18. Half-life: ~170–250 hours (Sub-Q)
19. Dose note: No community dosing exists; all figures are trial doses. Tablet doses are ~10× the injected dose, implying low oral absorption (inferred).
20. Most people take: Phase 3 uses 7.5, 12.5 or 17.5 mg Sub-Q weekly; Phase 2 used 2.5–15 mg. The oral tablet ran 15–120 mg daily, with 30 mg holding weight after a 90 mg start.
21. Phase 3 injection: 7.5, 12.5 or 17.5 mg · 1× weekly · 78 wk · Sub-Q · for VANQUISH obesity ± type 2 diabetes [S1] (verified)
22. Phase 2 injection: 2.5–15 mg · 1× weekly · 13 wk · Sub-Q · for VENTURE, adults with obesity [S2] [S3] (verified)
23. Oral tablet: 30–120 mg · 1× daily, titrated · 13 wk · Oral · for VENTURE-Oral; 15 mg did not beat placebo [S4] (verified)

# ATX-304
Page: https://baresignals.co/library/#/p/atx-304
Checked against Library v68, exported 2026-10-25

## Identity
1. Also called: O304, O-304, ATX304, ATX-304 Na salt
2. Origin: Not a peptide: small molecule
3. Legal and approval status: Investigational, not approved anywhere: Phase 1b done (2025), Phase 2 REWIRE-1 (muscle, lipids) and REWIRE-2 (weight loss) announced June 2026; MAD study restart pending after a July 2025 sponsor halt. As an unapproved drug it falls under WADA S0 (inferred); AMPK activators are also WADA S4 metabolic modulators (inferred).

## Summary
4. ATX-304 is an oral small molecule, not a peptide, that activates the cell's fuel sensor AMPK. It is pitched as an exercise mimetic that raises energy use rather than cutting appetite. A 2026 Phase 1b cut liver fat and raised resting metabolic rate 8% with little weight change. All human results are company press releases, and a dose-escalation study was paused by the sponsor in July 2025.
5. Punch line: Oral AMPK activator pitched as an exercise mimetic. Raises energy burn instead of cutting appetite; liver fat fell.
6. Used for: Liver fat, metabolic rate, insulin resistance

## Roles (what it is used for, strongest first)
7. Cellular energy: Raises cell energy use (AMPK)
8. Glucose & insulin: Lower fasting glucose in diabetics
9. Fat metabolism: Less liver and visceral fat
10. Muscle & performance: Better exercise capacity in mice
11. Organ function (backed only by animal or user reports): Liver fat down in Phase 1b
12. Heart & vessels (backed only by animal or user reports): Lower BP, better blood flow
13. Aging & senescence (backed only by animal or user reports): Reversed insulin resistance in old mice

## How it works
14. Keeps the cell's fuel sensor switched on · AMPK, protected from dephosphorylation · role Cellular energy
   ATX-304 activates AMPK, the cell's fuel sensor, and protects its switched-on, phosphorylated form from being turned off. AMPK stays active longer, pushing cells to burn fuel. Shown in cell and animal work, with early human trials.
15. Activates AMPK without draining ATP · ATP-independent AMPK activation · role Cellular energy
   Most AMPK activation happens when cells run low on ATP, their energy currency. ATX-304 is said by its developers to activate AMPK without draining ATP, so cells do not have to be stressed first. This mechanism comes from developer studies.
16. Pulls glucose into muscle without insulin · GLUT4 uptake via AMPK · role Glucose & insulin
   Active AMPK moves GLUT4, the glucose transporter, to the muscle cell surface. Muscle can then pull in glucose without insulin, as during exercise. A phase 2a trial in type 2 diabetics on metformin lowered fasting glucose.
17. Burns more fat in mitochondria · Mitochondrial proton conductance, fatty acid oxidation · role Fat metabolism
   AMPK raises fatty acid oxidation and mitochondrial proton conductance, so cells burn more fat and release more energy as heat. A 2026 phase 1b in people with obesity and prediabetes cut liver fat and raised resting metabolic rate.
18. Widens small blood vessels · Microvascular perfusion · role Heart & vessels
   ATX-304 widens small blood vessels and raises microvascular perfusion, the blood flow through tiny vessels in tissue. Better flow brings more oxygen and glucose to muscle. The 2017 phase 2a in type 2 diabetics showed raised microvascular flow and lower blood pressure.
19. Mechanism overview: ATX-304 (O304) is an oral small molecule that activates AMPK, the cell's energy sensor, across all its isoforms. Its developers say it does this without lowering ATP, by protecting the active, phosphorylated form of AMPK from being switched off, and that it acts mainly outside the brain. Active AMPK pushes GLUT4 to the muscle surface for insulin-independent glucose uptake, raises fatty acid oxidation and mitochondrial proton conductance, and so lifts energy use the way aerobic training does.

23. Most people take: Phase 1b used 400 mg once daily by mouth for 8 weeks plus an 8-week open extension; biohacker guides cite 200–400 mg a day. Oral only, no injection.

# MariTide
Page: https://baresignals.co/library/#/p/maritide
Checked against Library v68, exported 2026-10-25

## Identity
1. Also called: Maridebart cafraglutide, AMG 133, Mari-Tide
2. Origin: Lab-designed: antibody carrying two GLP-1 peptides
3. Legal and approval status: Investigational as of Oct 2026, not approved anywhere. Phase 3 MARITIME-1 and -2 (72 wk, obesity) ongoing with readouts expected 2027; CV, HF, sleep apnea, SWITCH and extension studies enrolling (Amgen, Aug 2026). Not named on the WADA list.

## Summary
4. MariTide is Amgen's antibody-peptide conjugate: an antibody that blocks the GIP receptor, carrying two GLP-1 agonist peptides. It is being developed as a monthly or less frequent weight-loss shot, with the antibody body giving it weeks-long action. Phase 2 showed up to 16% average weight loss at a year. Vomiting was heavy until a slower start was introduced, and a disputed bone density signal is under question.
5. Punch line: Amgen's monthly weight-loss shot: a GIP-blocking antibody carrying two GLP-1 peptides. Phase 2 reached about 16%.
6. Used for: Obesity, type 2 diabetes

## Roles (what it is used for, strongest first)
7. Appetite & satiety: Monthly hunger suppression
8. Glucose & insulin: HbA1c down 1.2–1.6 points
9. Fat metabolism: Up to ~20% weight loss
10. Heart & vessels: CV and heart failure trials
11. Sleep & rhythms (backed only by animal or user reports): Sleep apnea trials running
12. Bone & cartilage (backed only by animal or user reports): Bone density question, disputed

## How it works
13. Quiets hunger · GLP-1 receptor agonism (two peptides) · role Appetite & satiety
   Two GLP-1 analogue peptides fused onto the antibody activate GLP-1 receptors in the brain's appetite centres. Hunger drops and the stomach slows. This drove most of the weight loss seen in the Phase 2 human trial.
14. Blocks GIP signalling · Anti-GIPR antagonist antibody · role Fat metabolism
   The antibody part blocks the GIP receptor rather than activating it, the opposite of tirzepatide. Animal work and human genetics both linked lower GIP signalling to less weight gain. Why blocking and activating GIP both help weight loss is still debated.
15. Lowers blood sugar · GLP-1R on beta cells · role Glucose & insulin
   GLP-1 receptors on pancreatic beta cells raise insulin when glucose is high. In the type 2 diabetes group of the Phase 2 human trial, HbA1c improved alongside weight loss. The glucose-dependent action keeps the risk of lows small.
16. Antibody body gives weeks-long life · IgG, FcRn recycling · role Appetite & satiety
   The drug is built on a human IgG antibody, which the body recycles through the FcRn receptor instead of breaking down. That gives a half-life of about three weeks. It allows monthly or even less frequent dosing, which held weight loss in the year-two extension.
17. Mechanism overview: MariTide is a bispecific antibody-peptide conjugate. A fully human monoclonal antibody antagonises the GIP receptor, and two GLP-1 analogue peptides fused to it by amino-acid linkers activate the GLP-1 receptor. GLP-1 agonism cuts appetite, slows the stomach and raises glucose-dependent insulin. Blocking GIPR, rather than activating it like tirzepatide, also reduced weight in animal and human genetics work; why both approaches work is still debated. The antibody frame gives a half-life of about three weeks, allowing monthly or less frequent dosing.

## Dosage (community reported unless tagged)
18. Typical: Phase 3: 21 → 35 → 70 mg escalation to target dose · every 4 weeks; 8–12 weeks being tested · cycle Trial only (52–72 wk) · route Sub-Q (verified)
19. Half-life: ~21 days (phase 1, reported)
20. Dose note: Phase 3 target doses are not public. No community dosing exists.
21. Most people take: Trial only. Phase 2 used 140–420 mg every 4 weeks or 420 mg every 8 weeks; phase 3 starts at 21 mg and steps to 35 then 70 mg over 8 weeks before a target dose. Maintenance at monthly or quarterly intervals is under study.
22. Phase 2: 140–420 mg · every 4 wk (420 mg also every 8 wk) · 52 wk · Sub-Q · for 592 adults with obesity ± T2D [S1] (verified)
23. Phase 3 escalation: 21 → 35 → 70 mg · stepped over 8 wk, then target dose · 72 wk · Sub-Q · for MARITIME-1 and -2 [S2] (verified)
24. Maintenance: lower monthly or quarterly · every 4–12 wk · year two · Sub-Q · for phase 2 part 2; SWITCH from sema/tirz [S3] [S4] (reported)

## What people report
25. No meaningful grey-market use: it is a large antibody that cannot be made as a cheap synthetic peptide.
26. Liked / worked: Up to 16.2% loss at 52 wk (ITT), ~20% on treatment
27. Liked / worked: HbA1c down 1.2–1.6 points
28. Liked / worked: Loss held a second year on fewer doses
29. Liked / worked: Dose escalation cut GI dropouts
30. What worked: Up to 16.2% weight loss at 52 weeks (about 20% in people who stayed on drug) without diabetes, up to 12.3% with diabetes; HbA1c fell 1.2–1.6 points. Most kept the loss a further year on lower monthly or quarterly doses.
31. Went wrong / did not work: Vomiting 43–92% across phase 2 arms
32. Went wrong / did not work: 12–27% quit for GI effects without escalation
33. Went wrong / did not work: Phase 2 headline judged underwhelming by investors
34. Went wrong / did not work: Bone density signal raised, then denied
35. What went wrong: Vomiting in 43–92% of phase 2 arms; 12–27% quit for GI effects when started at full dose. A leaked phase 1 figure showed about 4% bone density loss at 420 mg, which Amgen says is not linked to the drug.
36. Most reported: Not available outside trials
37. Most reported: Monthly dosing is the draw

## What has been tested
38. Fat metabolism: Obesity, phase 1 and 52-wk phase 2 (human)
39. Glucose & insulin: Type 2 diabetes cohort (human)
40. Heart & vessels: CV and HF outcome trials (ongoing) (human)
41. Sleep & rhythms: Obstructive sleep apnea trials (ongoing) (human)
42. Phase 1 (Nature Metabolism 2024), a 592-person 52-week phase 2 (NEJM 2025) plus a year-two maintenance extension; the phase 3 MARITIME program has nine studies running.
43. What it helps: Phase 2 showed up to 16% average weight loss at a year, about 20% in people who stayed on drug, and 12% in type 2 diabetes with better HbA1c. Most kept the weight off for a further year on lower monthly or quarterly doses. Vomiting was the main problem until a slower start was introduced. It is being tested in heart disease, heart failure and sleep apnea; there is no grey-market use.
44. Trial: active · Phase 3 · heart disease with obesity · NCT07037433 · Amgen. Amgen's monthly shot is in a large MARITIME Phase 3 program, including a cardiovascular outcomes trial recruiting through 2028. (checked 2026-10-23) [S5] (verified)

## Who shouldn't take it
45. Personal or family history of MTC or MEN2: Causes thyroid C-cell tumours in rodents; boxed warning and contraindication on the label. (inferred)
46. Anyone booked for surgery, endoscopy or sedation: Food can stay in the stomach for days and be inhaled into the lungs under anaesthesia. (inferred)
47. People who struggle with vomiting at first dose: High first-dose vomiting rates in phase 2. (reported)

## Synergies (paired with)
48. Semaglutide: Semaglutide is a weekly GLP-1 agonist, while MariTide adds GIP receptor blocking and lasts weeks. They hit the same GLP-1 target, so they are alternatives, not a stack. Combining them has not been tested.
49. Tirzepatide: Tirzepatide activates the GIP receptor and MariTide blocks it, while both activate GLP-1. They are compared as rival approaches to the same goal. Using them together makes little pharmacological sense and has not been tested.

## Where it comes from
50. Amgen's antibody-peptide conjugate: an antibody that blocks the GIP receptor, carrying two GLP-1 agonist peptides. The antibody body lets it last weeks, so dosing is monthly or less.
51. First studied for: Obesity, with and without type 2 diabetes.
52. Name story: The INN pairs two stems: -bart, the 2021 stem for engineered full-length antibodies, and cafraglutide, carrying -glutide for GLP-1 analogues. MariTide is Amgen's own nickname; the meaning of 'Mari' is not explained publicly. [S6] (inferred)

# GHK-Cu + KPV
Page: https://baresignals.co/library/#/p/ghk-cu-kpv
Checked against Library v68, exported 2026-10-25

## Identity
1. Also called: GHK-Cu/KPV 60 mg, GHK-Cu/KPV 70 mg (Beauty Blend), copper peptide + KPV, KLOW without BPC-157 and TB-500
2. Origin: Blend of 2 peptides
3. Legal and approval status: US: not approved. GHK-Cu (injectable) and KPV were removed from FDA Category 2 on 15 Apr 2026; KPV won an 8-6-1 PCAC vote in July 2026, GHK-Cu goes to a panel before end of Feb 2027. No blend has any approval. EU, UK, Australia: no approved product. WADA: both fall under S0.

## Summary
4. This blend combines the copper tripeptide GHK-Cu with KPV, an anti-inflammatory tripeptide, in one vial. People pair them so GHK-Cu supports collagen, skin and hair while KPV calms inflammation in skin and gut. Evidence is per component, with small topical human skin trials for GHK-Cu and mouse colitis models for KPV, and nobody has tested the pair.
5. Punch line: KLOW minus BPC-157 and TB-500. Copper peptide rebuilds collagen and skin; KPV calms skin and gut inflammation.
6. Used for: Skin quality, scars, inflamed skin and gut

## Roles (what it is used for, strongest first)
7. Skin & aesthetics: Collagen and skin repair from GHK-Cu
8. Inflammatory signaling: KPV switches off inflammation signals
9. Tissue repair: Wound and scar closure
10. Digestive & gut: KPV calms colitis in mice
11. Hair (backed only by animal or user reports): GHK-Cu used for hair density
12. Immunity (backed only by animal or user reports): Steadies overreacting immune cells

## How it works
13. Turns on collagen building in skin · Fibroblast collagen and decorin synthesis · role Skin & aesthetics
   GHK-Cu signals fibroblasts to make collagen, decorin and glycosaminoglycans, the building blocks of skin matrix. It also shifts the balance between matrix-remodelling enzymes and their inhibitors. This is shown in cell and animal studies and small topical human skin trials.
14. Carries copper to healing tissue · Cu(II) bound to Gly-His-Lys · role Tissue repair
   GHK-Cu binds a copper ion tightly and delivers it to rebuilding tissue, where copper enzymes cross-link collagen. KPV has no His, Met or Asn, so it does not compete for that copper. The two can sit in one vial without disturbing the copper complex.
15. Blocks a key inflammation switch · NF-κB down · role Inflammatory signaling
   KPV, residues 11 to 13 of alpha-MSH, blocks activation of NF-κB, the main switch for inflammatory genes. It does this without the MC1R tanning receptor. This is shown in cell studies and mouse colitis models, with no human trial.
16. Gets into gut and immune cells · PepT1 transporter · role Digestive & gut
   KPV enters gut and immune cells through PepT1, a transporter for small peptides in the gut lining. That lets it act inside the cells driving inflammation. In mice this eased colitis and helped the colon lining heal.
17. Mechanism overview: GHK-Cu is the Gly-His-Lys tripeptide holding a Cu(II) ion; it raises collagen, decorin and glycosaminoglycan synthesis in fibroblasts and shifts the balance of matrix metalloproteinases and their inhibitors. KPV is Lys-Pro-Val, residues 11 to 13 of alpha-MSH; it enters cells by PepT1 and blocks NF-κB activation independent of MC1R. The pair covers matrix rebuilding (GHK-Cu) and inflammation control (KPV). KPV has no His, Met or Asn, so it does not compete for copper and is chemically quiet beside Cu-GHK.

## What is inside the blend
18. GHK-Cu: 50 mg · Collagen, skin and hair repair; carries copper
19. KPV: 10 mg · Switches down inflammation in skin and gut
20. Most common ratio: GHK-Cu 50 · KPV 10 = 60 mg (10 of 15 listings)
21. Other ratio seen: GHK-Cu 50 · KPV 20 ("Beauty Blend") = 70 mg (5 listings, mostly one factory's naming)
22. Other ratio seen: GHK-Cu 25 · KPV 5 = 30 mg (reported for some boutique sellers, no listing seen)
23. Version Most listings: GHK-Cu 50 · KPV 10 = 60 mg
24. Version Beauty Blend: GHK-Cu 50 · KPV 20 = 70 mg
25. Why GHK-Cu is in it: Matrix rebuilding: collagen, skin firmness, hair; KPV does none of this
26. Why KPV is in it: Direct anti-inflammatory signal (NF-κB) for flares, gut and skin; GHK-Cu's anti-inflammatory effect is weaker and indirect
27. Mixing chemistry: KPV (Lys-Pro-Val) has no His, Met or Asn, so it does not grab copper or oxidise easily: the quietest partner GHK-Cu can have.
28. Mixing chemistry: Copper stays bound above about pH 4; a blue solution means the complex is intact, a green or brown shift suggests copper has come off.
29. Mixing chemistry: Keep vitamin C, glutathione and other reducers out of the vial and syringe: copper plus a reducer drives oxidation.
30. Mixing chemistry: GHK-Cu over-fill of around 20% has been seen on KLOW lab certificates; ask for per-component mg, not one purity number.
31. Self-mixing: Mixing separate vials lets you change the 5:1 ratio, but pulls acidic KPV or BPC-style acetate liquid into the copper vial, which can lower pH toward the zone where copper loosens.

## Dosage (community reported unless tagged)
32. Typical: 1–2 mg GHK-Cu equivalent · 1× daily · cycle 4–8 weeks · route Sub-Q (reported)
33. Half-life: per component
34. Most people take: No standard blend dose. People size it on GHK-Cu: 60 mg in 3 mL, 10 units gives about 1.7 mg GHK-Cu and 0.33 mg KPV.

## What people report
35. Usually Sub-Q, once daily, sized off GHK-Cu (1 to 2 mg). At that size KPV lands at 0.2 to 0.4 mg, the low end of its usual range (0.4 to 0.8 mg on the 50 + 20 vial). Some users split it into two daily shots to soften the sting.
36. Liked / worked: Each component has animal or small human data
37. Liked / worked: KPV said to soften GHK-Cu sting
38. Liked / worked: Covers skin repair and inflammation in one shot
39. What worked: No blend-specific report pool. Users of the parent KLOW blend and of each component report smoother, calmer skin, faster scar and wound closure, and calmer gut and eczema flares. KPV is often added because it is said to reduce the injection sting of GHK-Cu.
40. Went wrong / did not work: Never tested as a pair
41. Went wrong / did not work: GHK-Cu sting and flushing with every dose
42. Went wrong / did not work: No reconstituted stability data
43. What went wrong: GHK-Cu dominates the vial (50 of 60 mg), so the injection sting, skin flushing and tiredness people report from copper peptide come with every dose. KPV users report early headache or flu-like feeling at low doses. No human efficacy data for either peptide injected, and none for the pair.
44. Most reported: Dose set by GHK-Cu, 1 to 2 mg
45. Most reported: Some split into two shots a day
46. Most reported: Bought as a cheaper KLOW alternative

## What has been tested
47. Never tested as a combination in animals or people. GHK-Cu has cell, animal and small topical human skin studies; KPV has mouse colitis and cell studies. No published stability study of the two reconstituted together; lab certificates exist for the larger KLOW blend, not this pair.
48. What it helps: Evidence is per component. GHK-Cu: cell and animal wound studies and small topical human skin trials. KPV: mouse colitis models, no human trial. No study has tested them together; users report calmer, smoother skin and fewer flares, mostly from the related KLOW blend.

## Who shouldn't take it
49. Wilson's disease or copper overload: Each dose delivers copper; people who cannot clear copper accumulate it in liver and brain. (inferred)
50. People with IBD on biologics or immunosuppressants: KPV damps NF-kB signalling; stacking it onto immune drugs is untested. (inferred)
51. People with cholestatic liver disease: Copper leaves the body through bile; PBC, PSC and bile duct blockage raise body copper. (inferred)
52. People fighting an active infection: Blunting inflammation can blunt the response clearing the infection. (inferred)

## Synergies (paired with)
53. BPC-157: BPC-157 adds vessel growth, tendon and gut repair, while this blend covers skin matrix and inflammation control. Adding it moves toward the KLOW blend. No study has tested these together, so it is user logic, not trial data.
54. Thymosin Beta-4: Thymosin beta-4 adds cell migration and anti-inflammatory action for deeper wounds. Combined with this blend and BPC-157 it forms the KLOW stack. The combination has not been tested in animals or people.
55. GHK-Cu: This blend already contains GHK-Cu, so adding more raises the collagen and copper share, and with it the copper load. People do this for scars or hair. There is no data on extra benefit.
56. KPV: This blend already contains KPV, so adding more raises the NF-κB-blocking anti-inflammatory share. People do this for gut or skin flares. There is no data on extra benefit.

## Where it comes from
57. A two-peptide vial: the copper tripeptide GHK-Cu (50 mg) with the anti-inflammatory tripeptide KPV (10 mg); a 50 + 20 mg version also sells. It is KLOW with BPC-157 and TB-500 taken out.
58. First studied for: Sold as a skin and calming blend: GHK-Cu for collagen, skin and hair, KPV to switch down inflammation in skin and gut.
59. 1973: GHK-Cu isolated from human plasma (Pickart)
60. 1990s to 2000s: KPV studied as the calming tail of alpha-MSH
61. 2020s: GLOW and KLOW blends spread; the two-peptide GHK-Cu + KPV vial follows
62. Apr 2026: Both removed from FDA Category 2
63. Today: Sold as a skin and inflammation blend, mostly 50 + 10 mg (60 mg); 50 + 20 also sold

# HMG
Page: https://baresignals.co/library/#/p/hmg
Checked against Library v68, exported 2026-10-25

## Identity
1. Also called: human menopausal gonadotropin, menotropins, menotrophin, Menopur, Pergonal (historic), Repronex, Humegon, Menogon
2. Origin: Made by the body: FSH and LH purified from postmenopausal urine
3. Shown with an FDA approved badge
4. Legal and approval status: FDA-approved as Menopur (menotropins, first US approval 1975); a biologic since Mar 2020. EMA lists the Menopur 1200 IU shortage as resolved (updated Apr 2026). WADA 2026 S2: prohibited.

## Summary
5. HMG (menotropins, Menopur) is a mix of FSH and LH extracted from the urine of postmenopausal women. It is approved to grow follicles for ovulation induction and IVF, and it is used in men with low gonadotropins to restart sperm production, usually added to hCG. Risks in women include ovarian hyperstimulation and multiple pregnancies, and male recovery can take up to two years.
6. Punch line: FSH plus LH purified from postmenopausal urine. Grows follicles for IVF and restarts sperm when hCG alone fails.
7. Used for: IVF follicle growth, male spermatogenesis restart

## Roles (what it is used for, strongest first)
8. Reproductive: Grows follicles, restarts sperm
9. Endocrine & growth: Supplies FSH and LH
10. Connection & desire: LH activity lifts testosterone
11. Mood: Mood swings during stimulation

## How it works
12. Grows egg follicles · FSH receptor, granulosa cells · role Reproductive
   The FSH in menotropins binds FSH receptors on granulosa cells, which line the egg follicles in the ovary. This recruits and grows several follicles at once. Its approved job is driving follicle growth in IVF cycles.
13. Drives sperm production with testosterone · FSH receptor, Sertoli cells · role Reproductive
   In the testes, FSH binds Sertoli cells, which nurse developing sperm. Together with high local testosterone, this drives spermatogenesis. Small studies in men support adding it to hCG when sperm does not return.
14. LH activity makes testosterone · LHCGR, Leydig and theca cells · role Endocrine & growth
   The LH activity in menotropins, mostly from hCG according to the label, binds LHCGR on Leydig and theca cells. These cells then make more testosterone and other androgens. In men it fills the gap hCG alone leaves by adding FSH beside the LH signal.
15. Estrogen climbs as follicles grow · Aromatase, estradiol · role Mood
   Androgens from theca cells are turned into estradiol by aromatase in the growing follicles. The more follicles grow, the higher estradiol climbs. Clinicians track this rise to time IVF and avoid overstimulation.
16. Mechanism overview: Menotropins is a purified mix of follicle-stimulating hormone and luteinizing-hormone activity from postmenopausal urine; the label notes most of the LH activity comes from hCG. FSH binds FSH receptors on ovarian granulosa cells to recruit and grow follicles, and on testicular Sertoli cells to support spermatogenesis. The LH component binds LHCGR on theca and Leydig cells, raising androgen and estradiol production. In men it fills the gap hCG leaves, since hCG supplies only LH-like signalling.

## Dosage (community reported unless tagged)
17. Typical: 225 IU/day (IVF); 75 IU (men, off-label) · daily (IVF); every other day to 3×/week (men) · cycle ≤20 days per IVF cycle; months in men · route Sub-Q (label), IM (verified)
18. Half-life: FSH ~11–13 h
19. Most people take: IVF: 225 IU SC daily, adjust by ≤150 IU, max 450 IU/day, ≤20 days. Men: 75 IU every other day added to hCG if azoospermia persists (review protocol for FSH); community uses 75–150 IU 2–3×/week.

## What people report
20. Used by men coming off TRT or steroids, usually layered on hCG at 75 IU a few times a week to supply the FSH hCG lacks. First-hand reports are few.
21. Liked / worked: Multiple follicle growth for IVF
22. Liked / worked: Restores sperm when hCG alone fails
23. Liked / worked: Long fertility track record
24. What worked: Grows multiple follicles for IVF; first pregnancy from extracted gonadotropins in 1962. In men, adding FSH to hCG can restart sperm when hCG alone fails.
25. Went wrong / did not work: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome
26. Went wrong / did not work: Multiple pregnancies
27. Went wrong / did not work: Blood clots (label)
28. Went wrong / did not work: Slow male recovery, up to 2 years
29. What went wrong: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome, multiple pregnancies and blood clots in women (label). Male sperm recovery can take up to two years.
30. Most reported: Used on top of hCG for FSH
31. Most reported: Post-TRT fertility restarts
32. Most reported: Few detailed first-hand reports

## What has been tested
33. Reproductive: IVF and ovulation induction (human)
34. Reproductive: Sperm recovery added to hCG (human)
35. Decades of fertility use and IVF trials; in men, small studies adding FSH or hMG to hCG for azoospermia.
36. What it helps: Its approved job is growing multiple follicles in IVF cycles. In men with low gonadotropins, or after TRT and steroids, clinicians add FSH or hMG to hCG when sperm does not return on hCG alone. The male data are small studies and reviews. Community use is mostly men restoring fertility; reports are sparse.
37. Trial: active · IVF ovarian stimulation · Ferring and academic centres. Approved as Menopur; used as a standard arm in many ongoing IVF trials, though no specific recruiting hMG record was confirmed here. (checked 2026-10-23) [S1] (inferred)

## Who shouldn't take it
38. Women with PCOS or prior ovarian hyperstimulation: These women overrespond and are most at risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome. (verified)
39. People with clotting history: Hyperstimulation thickens the blood and raises the risk of clots; label warns. (verified)
40. Pituitary tumour, pituitary surgery or brain radiation: Label contraindicates pituitary or hypothalamic tumours. (verified)

## Synergies (paired with)
41. HCG: HCG supplies the LH signal that keeps testosterone high inside the testes, and HMG adds FSH for Sertoli cells and sperm production. This is a clinical combination for men whose sperm does not return on hCG alone, backed by small studies and reviews.
42. Gonadorelin: Gonadorelin pulses the pituitary to release its own LH and FSH, while HMG supplies FSH and LH activity directly. They overlap in goal, so pairing them is user logic for fertility restarts, not trial data.
43. Kisspeptin-10: Kisspeptin-10 prompts the brain to restart GnRH and LH release, and HMG supplies FSH for sperm production at the testes. People use the logic of working top and bottom of the axis, but the pair has not been tested together.

## Where it comes from
44. FSH and LH extracted from the urine of postmenopausal women, whose bodies pour these hormones out once the ovaries stop. Each 75 IU vial carries 75 IU FSH and 75 IU LH activity.
45. First studied for: Ovulation induction and IVF; also used to start sperm production in men with low gonadotropins.
46. Name story: Hormones from postmenopausal urine, first purified by Piero Donini in Italy. Early supply came from convents with a quiet papal blessing: about 100 nuns gave 30,000 litres for 100 mg. The brand Pergonal means "per gonadi", for the gonads. [S2] (reported)
47. 1940s–50s: Donini extracts FSH and LH from postmenopausal urine
48. 1962: First birth after extracted gonadotropins (Pergonal)
49. 1975: First US approval of menotropins
50. Mar 2020: Reclassified as a biologic; compounding cut off
51. 2023–2025: Menopur shortage in Europe, resolved (EMA)

# NAD+ + MOTS-c + 5-Amino-1MQ
Page: https://baresignals.co/library/#/p/mitoprime
Checked against Library v68, exported 2026-10-25

## Identity
1. Also called: MitoPrime, NAD+ / MOTS-c / 5-Amino-1MQ blend, NAD+ + MOTS-c + 5-Amino-1MQ, Mito blend, MOTS-c + NAD+ + 5-Amino 120 mg
2. Origin: Blend: 1 peptide + 1 small molecule + coenzyme
3. Legal and approval status: No approved product anywhere. US: NAD+ is compounded and sold as a supplement; MOTS-c and 5-Amino-1MQ are unapproved research chemicals (MOTS-c was recommended by the July 2026 FDA compounding panel, no rule yet). WADA: AMPK activators are banned under S4 metabolic modulators, which covers MOTS-c (inferred); the blend is not safe for tested sport.

## Summary
4. Mitoprime is a one-vial injectable mix of NAD+ (the cell's energy coenzyme), MOTS-c (a peptide coded by mitochondrial DNA) and 5-Amino-1MQ (a small molecule that blocks the fat-cell enzyme NNMT). People take it for energy and fat loss during a diet. Evidence is mostly in mice per component, the blend has no trial, and the vial's amounts fall below each part's usual dose.
5. Punch line: Mitochondria in one vial. NAD+ and MOTS-c fuel energy while 5-Amino-1MQ blocks fat storage; dosed through a diet.
6. Used for: Energy and fat loss support, often alongside a GLP-1 or cardio

## Roles (what it is used for, strongest first)
7. Cellular energy: NAD+ and MOTS-c both aim at mitochondria
8. Fat metabolism: 5-Amino-1MQ and MOTS-c cut fat gain in mice
9. Glucose & insulin: MOTS-c improves insulin response in mice
10. Drive & mental stamina: Users take it for energy during a diet
11. Muscle & performance (backed only by animal or user reports): MOTS-c studied for exercise capacity
12. Aging & senescence (backed only by animal or user reports): NAD+ falls with age
13. DNA & telomeres (backed only by animal or user reports): NAD+ feeds DNA-repair enzymes

## How it works
14. Refills the cell's energy coenzyme · NAD+ for sirtuins, PARPs, electron transport · role Cellular energy
   NAD+ is the coenzyme that carries electrons through glycolysis and the electron transport chain, and the fuel for sirtuins and PARPs. Supplying it aims to refill pools that fall with age and stress. Human studies mainly show raised blood levels, not proven fat loss or energy gains.
15. Feeds DNA-repair enzymes · PARP substrate · role DNA & telomeres
   PARPs are DNA repair enzymes that use up NAD+ every time they mark damaged DNA for repair. More NAD+ keeps them supplied without draining the energy pool. This is established cell biology; benefit from extra NAD+ in healthy people is not shown.
16. Mitochondrial signal that acts like exercise · MOTS-c, AMPK activation · role Cellular energy
   MOTS-c is a small peptide made from mitochondrial DNA that activates AMPK, the cell's energy sensor that also switches on during exercise. AMPK raises fat and sugar burning. In mice it resisted diet-induced fat gain; there are no human trials.
17. Better insulin response in muscle · MOTS-c, folate cycle, AICAR · role Glucose & insulin
   MOTS-c slows the folate cycle, which builds up AICAR, a natural AMPK activator. That increases glucose uptake into muscle and improves insulin response. This was shown in insulin-resistant mice; human data are lacking.
18. Stops fat cells wasting NAD+ precursors · NNMT inhibition · role Fat metabolism
   5-Amino-1MQ blocks NNMT, an enzyme in fat cells that uses up nicotinamide, an NAD+ precursor, and SAM methyl groups. With NNMT blocked, more of both stay available. In the blend, this is meant to slow NAD+ loss; it is shown in mouse and cell studies.
19. Shrank fat cells in obese mice · 5-Amino-1MQ, SAM sparing · role Fat metabolism
   By sparing NAD+ and SAM in fat cells, 5-Amino-1MQ raised their energy use and reduced fat cell size. Diet-induced obese mice lost fat mass without eating less. There are no human trials of this compound.
20. Mechanism overview: NAD+ is the hydride carrier for glycolysis and the electron transport chain and the substrate for sirtuins and PARPs. MOTS-c, a 16-residue peptide (MRWQEMGYIFYPRKLR) from the mitochondrial 12S rRNA region, inhibits the folate cycle, raises AICAR and activates AMPK, improving insulin sensitivity in mice. 5-Amino-1MQ is a quaternary methylquinolinium that inhibits nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT), which in adipose tissue drains nicotinamide and SAM; blocking it raised adipocyte NAD+ and reduced fat mass in obese mice. The blend pairs NAD+ supply with an NNMT block that should slow NAD+ precursor loss, plus a parallel AMPK signal. No study has tested whether the parts add up.

## What is inside the blend
21. NAD+: 100 mg · The energy coenzyme itself, the bulk of the vial
22. MOTS-c: 10 mg · Mitochondrial peptide signal, AMPK and insulin response
23. 5-Amino-1MQ: 10 mg · Blocks NNMT so fat cells keep NAD+ precursors
24. Most common ratio: NAD+ 100 · MOTS-c 10 · 5-Amino-1MQ 10 = 120 mg (12 of 12 listings (6 state the split, 6 sell 120 mg))
25. Version Common retail: NAD+ 100 · MOTS-c 10 · 5-Amino-1MQ 10 = 120 mg
26. Version Higher 5-Amino version: NAD+ 100 · 5-Amino-1MQ 50 · MOTS-c 10 = 160 mg
27. Why NAD+ is in it: Supplies the coenzyme directly
28. Why MOTS-c is in it: Adds a signalling peptide; the only part with an exercise-like effect
29. Why 5-Amino-1MQ is in it: Slows NAD+ precursor loss in fat cells
30. Mixing chemistry: NAD+ is 100 of the 120 mg, so it sets the vial's pH and saltiness.
31. Mixing chemistry: NAD+ breaks down faster at higher pH and in phosphate or HEPES buffers; peptides often prefer different buffers.
32. Mixing chemistry: MOTS-c carries 2 methionines and a tryptophan, the parts most prone to oxidation in liquid.
33. Mixing chemistry: 5-Amino-1MQ is a small charged molecule; no cross-reaction with NAD+ is known.
34. Mixing chemistry: No published stability data for the mixed vial after reconstitution.
35. Self-mixing: Mixing separate vials puts an unknown NAD+ pH onto MOTS-c for weeks; drawing each into one syringe just before injecting avoids most of that.

## Dosage (community reported unless tagged)
36. Typical: 10–20 units of a 120 mg vial in 2 mL · 3–4× weekly, morning, fasted · cycle Not stated · route Sub-Q (reported)
37. Half-life: per component
38. Most people take: No standard dose. Sellers size it by the NAD+ share: 10 to 20 units of a 120 mg vial in 2 mL gives NAD+ 5 to 10 mg and MOTS-c and 5-Amino-1MQ 0.5 to 1 mg each. Much lower per part than people use when dosing each one alone.

## What people report
39. Sub-Q, morning, fasted, before cardio or training, 3 to 4 times a week (seller protocol). A second retail version with 50 mg 5-Amino-1MQ is dosed 25 to 50 units daily from a 5 mL mix. NAD+ injections are known for a burning sting and flushing, so expect that from the NAD+ share.
40. Liked / worked: Each part cut fat or improved glucose in mice
41. Liked / worked: Seller reports more energy while dieting
42. Liked / worked: Convenient one-vial dosing
43. What worked: A seller newsletter (Sep 2025) reports the author 'felt more energetic while losing fat' on 10 to 20 units 3 to 4 times a week. Component animal data: MOTS-c and 5-Amino-1MQ each cut fat gain in obese mice; NAD+ improved glucose handling in animal work.
44. Went wrong / did not work: Never tested together, in any species
45. Went wrong / did not work: Each part far below its usual solo dose
46. Went wrong / did not work: No stability data on the mixed vial
47. What went wrong: No human data on the blend and almost no independent user reports. At the published draw sizes each part lands far below its own usual dose: 20 units gives about 10 mg NAD+ (usual 50 to 100 mg), 1 mg MOTS-c (usual 5 to 10 mg) and 1 mg 5-Amino-1MQ (usually taken orally at 50 to 100 mg).
48. Most reported: 10 to 20 units, 3 to 4× a week
49. Most reported: Morning, fasted, before training
50. Most reported: NAD+ share can sting and flush
51. Most reported: Often stacked with a GLP-1

## What has been tested
52. Fat metabolism: 5-Amino-1MQ in diet-induced obese mice (mouse)
53. Glucose & insulin: MOTS-c in insulin-resistant mice (mouse)
54. Cellular energy: NAD+ infusion and oral precursors (human)
55. Cellular energy: The three combined (none)
56. Nothing tests the combination. Components: NAD+ in human infusion and supplement studies; MOTS-c in mouse obesity and exercise models; 5-Amino-1MQ in diet-induced obese mice (mostly oral or injected alone). No stability study of the mixed vial exists.
57. What it helps: Evidence is per component and mostly animal. MOTS-c and 5-Amino-1MQ each reduced fat gain in obese mice; NAD+ is studied in humans mainly for blood levels, not fat loss. The blend has no trial and only seller reports of more energy while dieting.

## Who shouldn't take it
58. People with active or recent cancer: Tumours depend on NAD+ for growth and DNA repair. (reported)
59. Insulin or sulfonylurea users: Raises insulin sensitivity via AMPK; adding it to glucose-lowering drugs can drop sugar too far. (inferred)
60. People on PARP inhibitors (olaparib etc.): PARP enzymes use NAD+; extra NAD+ may work against these drugs. (inferred)
61. Drug-tested athletes: WADA S4.4 bans AMPK activators as metabolic modulators; MOTS-c works through AMPK. (inferred)

## Synergies (paired with)
62. SS-31: SS-31 sits in the inner mitochondrial membrane and steadies the energy machinery, an approved drug for Barth syndrome. The blend raises NAD+ and AMPK signalling. People pair them for mitochondrial energy; the pair has not been tested together.
63. SLU-PP-332: SLU-PP-332 switches on ERR, the receptors behind endurance genes, and builds mitochondria, while MOTS-c here activates AMPK. Both mimic exercise from different angles. Each has mouse data only, and the pair has not been tested.
64. BAM-15: BAM-15 makes mitochondria leak protons so fuel burns as heat, while the blend supplies NAD+ and an AMPK signal. People stack them for fat loss. Each has mouse data only; the pairing is user logic, not trial data.
65. L-Carnitine: L-carnitine carries fatty acids into mitochondria, the place where NAD+ and AMPK signalling push fat burning. People pair them for fat oxidation. Carnitine has small oral weight loss effects; the pair has not been tested.
66. Retatrutide: Retatrutide drives weight loss through three receptors, with large human trials. The blend is added for energy and fat metabolism while eating less. The pairing is user logic, not trial data.
67. Tirzepatide: Tirzepatide does the main weight loss work through GIP and GLP-1 receptors, with large human trials. Users add this blend for energy during the deficit. The pair has not been tested together.
68. Semaglutide: Semaglutide cuts appetite through the GLP-1 receptor and has large human trials. The blend is added to offset low energy while dieting. The pairing is user logic, not trial data.

## Where it comes from
69. A one-vial injectable mix of three compounds sold for mitochondria and fat loss: NAD+ (the cell's energy coenzyme), MOTS-c (a small peptide coded by mitochondrial DNA) and 5-Amino-1MQ (a small molecule that blocks the fat-cell enzyme NNMT). The common vial is 100 + 10 + 10 = 120 mg.
70. First studied for: Grey-market blend that appeared around 2025, marketed as a 'stable' all-in-one for energy during fat loss. Each part was studied alone; the mix never was.
71. Name story: A product name: 'Mito' for mitochondria, 'Prime' for priming them. The same name is used, unrelated, for an L-ergothioneine supplement ingredient and a mitochondrial vitamin formula, so searches mix them up. [S1] (reported)
72. 2013: 5-Amino-1MQ family identified as NNMT blockers; NNMT tied to obesity (inferred date)
73. 2015: MOTS-c discovered, coded in mitochondrial DNA
74. 2018: 5-Amino-1MQ shrinks fat in obese mice
75. 2025: Sold pre-mixed with NAD+ as a 120 mg vial
76. Today: Grey-market 'mito' blend for energy during fat loss

# Abaloparatide
Page: https://baresignals.co/library/#/p/abaloparatide
Checked against Library v68, exported 2026-10-25

## Identity
1. Also called: Tymlos, BA058, BIM-44058, Eladynos (EU), Abaloparatide-SC, Eladynos
2. Origin: Lab-modified natural chain: PTHrP(1–34) analogue
3. Sequence: AVSEHQLLHDKGKSIQDLRRRELLEKLLAKLHTA (34 amino acids). Position 29 is Aib, shown as A; C-terminal amide
4. Shown with an FDA approved badge
5. Legal and approval status: FDA-approved as Tymlos (women 2017, men Dec 2022); boxed warning removed Dec 2021; hypersensitivity label update Aug 2026. Earliest US generic entry estimated Oct 2027 (reported). Not on the WADA list by name.

## Summary
6. Abaloparatide (Tymlos) is a 34-amino-acid analogue of PTHrP, engineered to favour the receptor state that builds bone. A daily pen shot is FDA-approved for high-risk osteoporosis, and trials showed far fewer new spine fractures than placebo. Dizziness, nausea and high urine calcium recur, lifetime use is capped at two years, and a bone drug usually follows.
7. Punch line: Daily pen shot built on PTHrP, not PTH. Approved for high-risk osteoporosis; trials cut new spine fractures 86%.
8. Used for: Osteoporosis, low bone density

## Roles (what it is used for, strongest first)
9. Bone & cartilage: Builds new bone, fewer fractures
10. Tissue repair: Fracture healing interest
11. Endocrine & growth: Acts on the PTH receptor
12. Aging & senescence: Reverses age-related bone loss
13. Heart & vessels (backed only by animal or user reports): Dizziness, fast heartbeat after dose

## How it works
14. Pulses switch on bone-building cells · PTH1 receptor (PTH1R), RG conformation · role Bone & cartilage
   Abaloparatide is a PTHrP analogue that binds the PTH1 receptor and favours its RG conformation, a state that gives short bursts of cAMP signalling. Given as a daily pulse, this switches on osteoblasts, the bone-building cells. Phase 3 trials in people confirm the bone gains.
15. Builds more than it breaks down · Anabolic window, osteoblast > osteoclast · role Bone & cartilage
   Each pulse opens an anabolic window, where osteoblasts lay down new bone before osteoclasts, the bone-removing cells, catch up. Net bone is gained. In ACTIVE this cut new vertebral fractures in postmenopausal women, and ATOM showed density gains in men.
16. Less calcium spike than teriparatide · Transient cAMP signalling · role Endocrine & growth
   Because its cAMP signal is brief, it mobilises less calcium from bone and kidney than teriparatide. Blood calcium rises less as a result. High urine calcium can still occur and is one of the recurring problems.
17. Widens blood vessels briefly · Vascular PTH1R · role Heart & vessels
   PTH1 receptors also sit on blood vessels, and activating them relaxes the vessel wall. This causes a brief drop in blood pressure and a faster heartbeat after a dose. It explains the dizziness some people report.
18. Mechanism overview: Abaloparatide is a 34-residue synthetic analogue of parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP 1–34) with substitutions including an Aib at position 29. It binds the PTH1 receptor (PTH1R) and favours the RG conformation, which gives short cAMP bursts. Given as a daily pulse, this tilts bone remodelling towards osteoblasts laying down new bone before osteoclasts catch up, the so-called anabolic window, with less sustained calcium mobilisation than teriparatide. Vascular PTH1R activation explains the transient blood pressure drop and faster heartbeat.

## Dosage (community reported unless tagged)
19. Typical: 80 mcg · once daily · cycle Max 2 years lifetime, then antiresorptive · route Sub-Q (abdomen) (verified)
20. Half-life: ~1 h
21. Most people take: 80 mcg SC daily into the periumbilical abdomen, sitting or lying for early doses; up to 2 years lifetime, then denosumab or a bisphosphonate. A 300 mcg transdermal patch was tested but abandoned.

## What people report
22. Grey-market users take the clinical 80 mcg dose for bone density, usually then switching to an antiresorptive. Dizziness on early doses is the common report.
23. Liked / worked: 86% fewer new spine fractures
24. Liked / worked: Bone density up in spine and hip
25. Liked / worked: Works in men too
26. What worked: New vertebral fractures 0.6% vs 4.2% on placebo at 18 months (86% relative reduction), with gains in spine and hip density; approved for men to raise bone density.
27. Went wrong / did not work: Dizziness and orthostatic hypotension
28. Went wrong / did not work: Nausea, headache, palpitations
29. Went wrong / did not work: High urine calcium
30. Went wrong / did not work: 2-year lifetime cap
31. Went wrong / did not work: Patch version failed
32. What went wrong: Dizziness, nausea, headache, palpitations and orthostatic hypotension after doses; high urine calcium. Rat osteosarcoma; lifetime use capped at 2 years. The patch reached 7.1% vs 10.9% spine gain and was dropped.
33. Most reported: Dizziness on first doses
34. Most reported: Used before switching to denosumab
35. Most reported: Injection-site redness
36. Most reported: Few grey-market reports

## What has been tested
37. Bone & cartilage: Vertebral fractures, ACTIVE (human)
38. Bone & cartilage: Bone density in men, ATOM (human)
39. Tissue repair: Fracture healing (animal)
40. Phase 3 ACTIVE in postmenopausal women and ATOM in men; a microneedle patch failed its Phase 3 comparison.
41. What it helps: In ACTIVE it cut new vertebral fractures from 4.2% to 0.6% over 18 months in postmenopausal women and raised spine and hip density; ATOM showed density gains in men. It is used for high-risk osteoporosis, followed by an antiresorptive to keep the gain. Grey-market interest is small and mostly mirrors the clinical dose. Dizziness, nausea and high urine calcium are the recurring problems.
42. Trial: active · Phase 2 · spinal fusion in lumbar degenerative disease · NCT07587775. Approved as Tymlos; a new Phase 2 spine surgery study is not yet recruiting and two others are active but closed to enrollment. (checked 2026-10-23) [S1] (reported)

## Who shouldn't take it
43. Paget's disease, unexplained high ALP, prior bone radiation: Higher baseline osteosarcoma risk; label warns. (verified)
44. People prone to dizziness on standing: Orthostatic hypotension around first doses. (verified)
45. People with kidney stones or high urine calcium: It raises calcium in the urine, which can grow new stones. (verified)

## Where it comes from
46. A 34-amino-acid analogue of PTHrP, the parathyroid-hormone-related protein, engineered to favour the receptor state that builds bone over the one that drives calcium up. A daily pen shot that grows new bone rather than just slowing loss.
47. First studied for: Postmenopausal osteoporosis at high fracture risk; men added in 2022.
48. Name story: Discovered at Ipsen as BIM-44058, developed by Radius Health as BA058. The '-paratide' ending marks it as kin to teriparatide, but it copies PTHrP, the tumour-linked cousin of parathyroid hormone, with which it shares 76% of its sequence. [S2] (verified)
49. Apr 2017: FDA approves Tymlos for postmenopausal osteoporosis
50. Dec 2021: Rat-osteosarcoma boxed warning removed
51. Dec 2021: Patch misses non-inferiority in wearABLe; dropped Jun 2022
52. Dec 2022: Approved to raise bone density in men
53. Aug 2026: Label adds hypersensitivity reaction warning

# CBL-514
Page: https://baresignals.co/library/#/p/cbl-514
Checked against Library v68, exported 2026-10-25

## Identity
1. Also called: CBL514, CBL-514D (Dercum's formulation), Caliway fat-reduction injection
2. Origin: Not a peptide: small molecule (structure undisclosed)
3. Legal and approval status: Phase 3 as of Oct 2026: SUPREME-01 dosed its first participant Sep 2026 and SUPREME-02 IND cleared May 2026, results expected 2027. Not approved anywhere. Not named on the WADA list (inferred).

## Summary
4. CBL-514 is a first-in-class small-molecule injection from Taiwan's Caliway Biopharmaceuticals, not a peptide. It is aimed at non-surgical reduction of belly fat by triggering fat cells in the injected area to die by apoptosis. Company Phase 2b data show about three in four treated people improving a grade, against about one in five on placebo. All efficacy data come from the company, and injection-site pain is the main downside.
5. Punch line: Small-molecule injection that kills fat cells on the spot. Trials thinned belly fat; seen as a GLP-1 add-on.
6. Used for: Belly fat reduction, Dercum's disease

## Roles (what it is used for, strongest first)
7. Fat metabolism: Kills fat cells where injected
8. Skin & aesthetics: Smoother belly contour, cellulite
9. Pain & sensory: Less pain in Dercum's disease
10. Organ function: Less visceral fat on MRI

## How it works
11. Triggers fat cells to self-destruct · Adipocyte apoptosis, caspase-3 up · role Fat metabolism
   CBL-514 pushes fat cells into apoptosis, the orderly self-destruct program a cell runs on itself, and preclinical work showed caspase-3, the enzyme that carries out that program, rising. The cell is dismantled and cleared rather than just shrunk. In human trials this shows up as thinner, smaller fat layers at the injected site.
12. Tips cells toward death signals · Bax/Bcl-2 ratio up (preclinical) · role Fat metabolism
   Whether a cell lives or dies is partly set by the balance of Bax, which promotes death, against Bcl-2, which protects. CBL-514 shifted that balance toward Bax in preclinical studies, committing fat cells to apoptosis. This is lab and animal evidence for how it works, not something measured in people.
13. Kills cells without burning tissue · Non-necrotic, per company · role Skin & aesthetics
   Detergent-type fat dissolvers rupture cell membranes, which causes necrosis and inflammation in nearby tissue. CBL-514 is said to kill fat cells through apoptosis instead, so neighbouring skin and tissue are spared. That claim comes from the company; injection-site soreness is still the main reported downside in trials.
14. Fewer fat cells, so less regain in rodents · Combined with GLP-1/amylin drugs, preclinical · role Fat metabolism
   A fat cell that has died cannot be refilled, so fewer cells should mean less tissue to regain into. In rodents, adding CBL-514 to semaglutide or tirzepatide blunted weight regain. That is animal data only; regain after GLP-1 drugs has not been tested this way in people.
15. Mechanism overview: CBL-514 is an injected small molecule that drives adipocyte apoptosis, a programmed self-destruct in fat cells. In preclinical work it raised caspase-3 and the Bax/Bcl-2 ratio, the switches that commit a cell to apoptosis, and Caliway says it does this without necrosis of surrounding tissue, unlike detergent-type fat dissolvers that rupture membranes. Fewer fat cells means less tissue to refill, which is the basis for the company's claim that it blunts regain after GLP-1 drugs. The company reports no central nervous, heart or breathing effects.

## Dosage (community reported unless tagged)
16. Typical: Up to 600 mg per session · every 3 weeks · cycle Up to 4 sessions · route Sub-Q (into abdominal fat) (verified)
17. Half-life: Not published
18. Dose note: Only trial dosing exists; Phase 3 dose not published.
19. Most people take: Phase 2b: up to 600 mg per session, injected into the lower belly every 3 weeks for up to 4 sessions, injection count set by fat thickness. No community dose exists.
20. Phase 2b trial: up to 600 mg/session · every 3 weeks · up to 4 sessions (12 wk) · Sub-Q abdominal grid · for trial participants, BMI 22–30 [S1] [S2] (verified)

## What people report
21. Little first-hand use outside trials; interest comes from aesthetic medicine and GLP-1 users hoping to spot-treat stubborn fat or blunt regain.
22. Liked / worked: 76.7% vs 18.9% improved a fat grade
23. Liked / worked: About 27% thinner belly fat vs placebo
24. Liked / worked: Visceral fat down vs placebo on MRI
25. Liked / worked: Less Dercum's pain
26. What worked: In CBL-0204, 76.7% vs 18.9% on placebo improved at least one grade on a clinician fat scale, with 27% thinner belly fat vs placebo at 4 weeks; Dercum's pain fell vs placebo.
27. Went wrong / did not work: Injection-site pain, swelling, redness
28. Went wrong / did not work: Company-only data so far
29. Went wrong / did not work: Phase 3 not yet read out
30. What went wrong: Injection-site pain, swelling and redness; all efficacy data so far come from the company, and no peer-reviewed Phase 3 data exist yet.
31. Most reported: Seen as a spot-treatment add-on to GLP-1s
32. Most reported: Compared with Kybella and Lemon Bottle
33. Most reported: Few first-hand reports outside trials

## What has been tested
34. Fat metabolism: Abdominal subcutaneous fat, Phase 2b (human)
35. Organ function: Visceral fat on MRI, Phase 2 subgroup (human)
36. Pain & sensory: Dercum's disease pain, Phase 2 (human)
37. Fat metabolism: Weight regain with semaglutide/tirzepatide (animal)
38. About 10 completed company trials in 500+ people, including Phase 2b CBL-0204 (107 people) and CBL-0205 on belly fat, a Phase 2 in Dercum's disease and an MRI visceral-fat analysis; Phase 3 started 2026.
39. What it helps: Company Phase 2b data show about three in four treated people improving at least one grade on a belly-fat scale against about one in five on placebo, measurable fat thickness and volume loss within four weeks, and an MRI subgroup with visceral fat falling while placebo rose. A Phase 2 in Dercum's disease cut pain. Interest centres on non-surgical contouring and on pairing it with GLP-1 drugs; injection-site soreness is the main reported downside.
40. Trial: active · Phase 3 · belly fat reduction · NCT07526974 · Caliway Biopharmaceuticals. Two global Phase 3 fat dissolving injection trials (SUPREME-01 and 02) are starting in the US, Canada and Australia. (checked 2026-10-23) [S3] (verified)

## Who shouldn't take it
41. People on blood thinners: Multiple injections in fat; bruising. (inferred)

## Synergies (paired with)
42. Semaglutide: Semaglutide shrinks fat stores by cutting appetite, while CBL-514 removes fat cells at the injection site. The idea is that fewer fat cells leave less room to regain after stopping. That is shown only in rodents; the pair has not been tested together in people.
43. Tirzepatide: Tirzepatide drives broad weight loss through appetite and insulin effects, and CBL-514 targets local fat cells for removal. People pair them for overall loss plus contouring. Regain was blunted in rodents only; the pair has not been tested together in people.
44. Eloralintide: Eloralintide works on fullness through the amylin system, while CBL-514 removes fat cells locally. The pairing follows the same logic as with GLP-1 drugs and the company has mentioned amylin drugs in its preclinical work. It is user and preclinical logic, not human trial data.

## Where it comes from
45. A first-in-class small-molecule injection from Taiwan's Caliway Biopharmaceuticals that kills fat cells in the injected area by apoptosis rather than burning or dissolving them.
46. First studied for: Non-surgical reduction of abdominal subcutaneous fat; also cellulite and Dercum's disease (painful fatty lumps).
47. Name story: A Caliway development code: 'CBL' appears to stand for the company (Caliway Biopharmaceuticals Lab), while 514 has no public explanation. It has no INN yet. [S4] (inferred)
48. 2020–2021: Phase 1 and 2 belly-fat trials begin

50. Jul 2025: FDA clears Phase 3 SUPREME-01
51. May 2026: FDA clears second Phase 3, SUPREME-02

# Pemvidutide
Page: https://baresignals.co/library/#/p/pemvidutide
Checked against Library v68, exported 2026-10-25

## Identity
1. Also called: ALT-801, SP-1373
2. Origin: Lab-modified natural chain
3. Legal and approval status: Investigational, not approved anywhere: Phase 3 PERFORMA in MASH F2–F3 began Aug 2026 (52-week data expected 2029); FDA Breakthrough Therapy and Fast Track for MASH, Fast Track for AUD; ALD Phase 2 RESTORE readout 2H 2027. As an unapproved drug it falls under WADA S0 (inferred).

## Summary
4. Pemvidutide is Altimmune's balanced GLP-1 and glucagon dual agonist, a modified peptide given weekly. It is developed for fatty liver disease (MASH) and obesity, with the glucagon half burning liver fat and the GLP-1 half cutting appetite. In Phase 2, MASH resolved in 59% on drug versus 19% on placebo at 24 weeks, though the fibrosis biopsy endpoint missed. Nausea and vomiting drive dropouts.
5. Punch line: Liver-first weekly GLP-1 and glucagon dual agonist. MASH resolved in 59% at 24 weeks; Breakthrough status.
6. Used for: MASH, obesity, alcohol use disorder

## Roles (what it is used for, strongest first)
7. Organ function: Clears fat from the liver
8. Fat metabolism: Weight and liver fat loss
9. Reward & urges: Fewer heavy drinking days
10. Appetite & satiety: Lower hunger via GLP-1
11. Heart & vessels (backed only by animal or user reports): Lower LDL and triglycerides
12. Inflammatory signaling (backed only by animal or user reports): Resolves liver inflammation (MASH)

## How it works
13. Glucagon side burns fat inside the liver · Glucagon receptor, hepatocytes · role Organ function
   The glucagon side activates glucagon receptors on liver cells, raising fat burning and lowering new fat production in the liver. Liver fat falls faster than body weight as a result. In the IMPACT human trial, liver fat about halved and MASH resolved more often than on placebo.
14. GLP-1 side quiets hunger · GLP-1 receptor, brain · role Appetite & satiety
   The GLP-1 side activates GLP-1 receptors in the hypothalamus and brainstem, quieting hunger. It also offsets glucagon's pull on blood sugar. In the MOMENTUM human trial this produced weight loss that continued through 48 weeks.
15. Lipid tail rides albumin for weekly dosing · EuPort domain, albumin binding · role Fat metabolism
   A lipid domain called EuPort binds albumin in the blood, which slows absorption and clearance. The drug stays active long enough for one injection a week. This is a design feature rather than a separate effect on the body.
16. Dampens craving and reward circuits · Mesolimbic GLP-1R · role Reward & urges
   GLP-1 receptors in mesolimbic reward circuits appear to dull the pull of alcohol and other rewards. In the RECLAIM human trial, people with alcohol use disorder had fewer heavy drinking days. The exact brain mechanism in people is inferred from the GLP-1 class.
17. Lowers blood fats · Hepatic lipid metabolism · role Heart & vessels
   Glucagon receptor signalling changes how the liver handles fat, cutting fat production and sending out less. In early human trials LDL, triglycerides and apoB fell. These are blood markers; effects on heart events have not been studied.
18. Mechanism overview: Pemvidutide is a 1:1 balanced dual agonist of the GLP-1 and glucagon receptors, with a lipid EuPort domain that binds albumin and slows absorption for weekly dosing. Glucagon receptor signalling in hepatocytes raises fat oxidation and lowers fat synthesis in the liver, which is why liver fat falls faster than body weight. GLP-1 receptor signalling in the hypothalamus and brainstem cuts hunger and, in mesolimbic circuits, appears to blunt alcohol reward. The GLP-1 half also offsets the glucose-raising pull of glucagon.

## Dosage (community reported unless tagged)
19. Typical: 1.2–2.4 mg · once weekly · cycle Ongoing (trials 24–48 weeks) · route Sub-Q (verified)
20. Half-life: ~100 hours (reported)
21. Dose note: No community dosing exists to report; all figures are trial doses. Early trials started at full dose, but Phase 3 added titration for tolerability.
22. Most people take: Trials used 1.2 or 1.8 mg weekly Sub-Q for MASH, up to 2.4 mg for obesity and AUD; Phase 3 titrates monthly from 1.2 mg to 1.8 or 2.4 mg. No oral form.
23. MASH trial: 1.2–1.8 mg · 1× weekly · 24–48 wk · Sub-Q · for IMPACT Phase 2b, MASH with fibrosis [S1] [S2] (verified)
24. Obesity / AUD trial: 2.4 mg · 1× weekly · 24–48 wk · Sub-Q · for MOMENTUM obesity, RECLAIM alcohol use disorder [S3] [S4] (verified)
25. Phase 3 titration: 1.2 → 1.8 or 2.4 mg · 1× weekly, step up monthly · 52 wk+ · Sub-Q · for PERFORMA, MASH F2–F3 [S5] (verified)

## What people report
26. No real community use is documented; interest comes from trial readouts, mainly the liver data and the claim that it needs little or no dose titration.
27. Liked / worked: MASH resolution 59% vs 19% placebo at 24 weeks
28. Liked / worked: Liver fat down 45–55% at 48 weeks
29. Liked / worked: Up to 15.6% weight loss at 48 weeks
30. Liked / worked: Fewer heavy drinking days in AUD
31. Liked / worked: Breakthrough Therapy status for MASH
32. What worked: MASH resolution in 59% (1.2 mg) vs 19% placebo at 24 weeks, liver fat down about 45 to 55% at 48 weeks, up to 15.6% weight loss at 48 weeks in obesity, and fewer heavy drinking days in AUD.
33. Went wrong / did not work: Biopsy fibrosis endpoint missed at 24 weeks
34. Went wrong / did not work: Nausea, vomiting, constipation
35. Went wrong / did not work: ~19% quit high doses in obesity trial
36. Went wrong / did not work: One hyponatremia SAE possibly drug-related (RECLAIM)
37. What went wrong: The 24-week biopsy fibrosis endpoint missed significance (32 to 35% vs 26% placebo) and the stock fell about 59% that day; nausea, vomiting and constipation are common and 1.8 to 2.4 mg obesity doses had ~19% discontinuation for side effects.
38. Most reported: Little or no community use documented
39. Most reported: Interest centres on liver data
40. Most reported: Claimed lower need for titration
41. Most reported: Weight loss seen as modest vs tirzepatide

## What has been tested
42. Organ function: MASH resolution and liver fat, IMPACT (human)
43. Fat metabolism: Weight loss in obesity, MOMENTUM (human)
44. Reward & urges: Heavy drinking days in AUD, RECLAIM (human)
45. Heart & vessels: LDL, triglycerides, apoB in Phase 1 (human)
46. Phase 2b IMPACT in 212 biopsy-confirmed MASH patients (published in The Lancet), Phase 2 MOMENTUM in obesity, and Phase 2 RECLAIM in alcohol use disorder.
47. What it helps: In IMPACT, MASH resolved in 59% on 1.2 mg vs 19% on placebo at 24 weeks, liver fat fell about half by 48 weeks and non-invasive fibrosis markers improved, though the 24-week biopsy fibrosis endpoint missed. MOMENTUM showed up to 15.6% weight loss at 48 weeks, and RECLAIM cut heavy drinking days in alcohol use disorder. Interest is mainly from people with fatty liver; GI effects drive dropouts at higher doses.
48. Trial: active · Phase 3 · MASH liver disease · Altimmune. Phase 3 PERFORMA in MASH started mid 2026, and the alcohol liver disease Phase 2 finished enrolling in July 2026. (checked 2026-10-23) [S6] (reported)

## Who shouldn't take it
49. Personal or family history of MTC or MEN2: Causes thyroid C-cell tumours in rodents; boxed warning and contraindication on the label. (inferred)
50. Anyone booked for surgery, endoscopy or sedation: Food can stay in the stomach for days and be inhaled into the lungs under anaesthesia. (inferred)
51. People with arrhythmia or a fast resting pulse: The glucagon part of the drug pushes resting heart rate up. (inferred)

## Where it comes from
52. Altimmune's balanced 1:1 GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, bought in 2019 with Spitfire Pharma; the glucagon half works directly on the liver while the GLP-1 half cuts appetite.
53. First studied for: MASH (fatty liver inflammation) and obesity; later alcohol use disorder and alcohol-related liver disease.
54. Name story: It began as SP-1373 at Spitfire Pharma and became ALT-801 when Altimmune bought Spitfire in 2019. The "-dutide" ending is shared with other dual GLP-1/glucagon agonists such as survodutide and mazdutide. [S7] (verified)
55. 2019: Altimmune buys Spitfire Pharma and its SP-1373, renamed ALT-801
56. 2022: Phase 1: up to 10% weight loss in 12 weeks, big liver fat drops
57. Dec 2023: MOMENTUM: 15.6% weight loss at 48 weeks, ~19% quit on high doses
58. Jun 2025: IMPACT: MASH resolution hit, fibrosis biopsy missed; stock fell ~59%
59. Jul 2026: RECLAIM: fewer heavy drinking days in alcohol use disorder
60. Aug 2026: Phase 3 PERFORMA in MASH begins
