# PNC-27
Page: https://baresignals.co/library/#/p/pnc-27
Checked against Library v68, exported 2026-10-25

## Identity
1. Also called: PNC27, p53-penetratin peptide, p53(12-26)-penetratin
2. Origin: Lab-designed: p53 fragment fused to a cell-entry sequence
3. Sequence: PPLSQETFSDLWKLLKKWKMRRNQFWVKVQRG (32 amino acids). p53 residues 12 to 26 (the HDM-2 grip) followed by a 17-residue cell-entry tail the lab calls the membrane residency peptide, a reversed penetratin-like sequence; linear, 32 aa
4. Legal and approval status: Not approved anywhere and no trial on ClinicalTrials.gov as of 23 Oct 2026. FDA warned patients not to use it on 10 Jan 2017 after finding Variovorax paradoxus in an inhaled sample, then Ralstonia insidiosa in a second sample (27 Mar 2017). In 2021 an Alabama man pleaded guilty to conspiracy for making PNC-27 suppositories in his kitchen and selling them to patients and a Mexican clinic. Not named on the WADA list; falls under S0 (inferred).

## Summary
5. PNC-27 is a lab-designed peptide made from a piece of p53 fused to a cell-entry sequence, built at SUNY Downstate. It is thought to punch holes in cancer cells that display HDM-2 on their surface, and it kills cancer cells in dishes and some mouse models. No human trial exists, and the FDA warned in 2017 about contaminated products sold to patients.
6. Punch line: A p53 fragment with a cell-entry tag that punctures HDM-2 cancer cells in culture. No proven human benefit.
7. Used for: Cancer, experimental

## Roles (what it is used for, strongest first)
8. Cancer biology: Bursts cancer cells that carry HDM-2 on their surface

## How it works
9. Grabs HDM-2 sitting on cancer-cell surfaces · Membrane HDM-2 (MDM2), p53-binding region · role Cancer biology
   PNC-27 carries the stretch of p53 that grips HDM-2 (human MDM2). Many cancer cells display HDM-2 in their outer membrane, which normal cells mostly do not. That gives the peptide a cancer-cell target, and normal cells forced to carry membrane HDM-2 became sensitive in cell studies.
10. Pairs up into pores so the cell bursts · Transmembrane pore, necrosis (poptosis) · role Cancer biology
   Once bound to membrane HDM-2, the complexes pair up and form pores through the cell membrane. The cell leaks and bursts by necrosis rather than the orderly death of apoptosis. The lab calls this poptosis, and it has been shown in cancer cell lines and fresh tumour cells from two patients.
11. Also gets inside and damages the cell's power plants · Mitochondrial membrane disruption · role Cancer biology
   A 2024 paper reports a second route: the peptide also gets inside cancer cells and breaks the membranes of mitochondria, the cell's energy plants. Damaged mitochondria push the cell further toward death. This comes from cell studies only.
12. Works even where p53 is lost · p53-independent killing · role Cancer biology
   Because killing runs through membrane pores rather than switching on p53 itself, it does not need working p53. It killed p53-null cancer cells in culture, which matters since many tumours lose p53. Mouse data are limited, and no human trial has ever been run.
13. Mechanism overview: PNC-27 joins residues 12 to 26 of p53, the region that binds HDM-2 (human MDM2), to a 17-residue cell-entry sequence the lab calls the membrane residency peptide. Many cancer cells, unlike normal cells, display HDM-2 in their outer membrane. PNC-27 binds that membrane HDM-2 in the same helix shape p53 uses, the complexes pair into transmembrane pores, and the cell bursts by necrosis rather than apoptosis, so it works even in p53-null cells. Normal cells forced to carry membrane HDM-2 become sensitive, which supports the target. A 2024 paper adds a second route: the peptide enters cancer cells and breaks mitochondrial membranes. The authors call the whole process poptosis.

## Dosage (community reported unless tagged)
14. Typical: No human dose established; vendor sheets list 100–500 mcg · Daily to 3× weekly (vendor sheets) · cycle 8–12 weeks (vendor sheets) · route Sub-Q; nebulised, IV, suppository sold by clinics (reported)
15. Half-life: Unknown in humans
16. Most people take: No human dose exists. The numbers in circulation come from vendor sheets, not user logs: 200 to 300 mcg Sub-Q three times a week, or 100 to 500 mcg daily for 8 to 12 weeks. Clinics have sold nebulised, IV and suppository forms at undisclosed doses. For scale, the AML mouse study used 40 mg/kg a day by injection into the belly.

## What people report
17. Real-world use is almost entirely cancer patients buying through alternative clinics or online, as nebulised solution, IV solution and vaginal or rectal suppositories. Public user accounts are few: aggregators log 2 to 3 reports with no outcome data, a 2026 blog comment describes a husband with stage 4 lymphoma on 20-day cycles reporting unspecified results, and a 2025 pet-owner blog injected it near a dog's tumour with no measured result. The only medical case report is a 2017 abstract of massive GI bleeding during experimental use, cause unconfirmed.
18. Liked / worked: Kills HDM-2-positive cancer cells in culture within hours
19. Liked / worked: Spares matching normal cells in culture
20. Liked / worked: Works without functional p53
21. Liked / worked: Modestly longer survival in AML mice (independent lab)
22. What worked: In dishes it kills cancer cells within hours while sparing matching normal cells, and it works whether p53 is normal, mutant or missing. In mice, PNC-28 destroyed pancreatic tumours placed in the belly, and PNC-27 lengthened AML survival (median 54 vs about 41 days) and cut leukaemia stem cells. Ketone salts lowered the dose needed in cell work.
23. Went wrong / did not work: No human trial or human dose
24. Went wrong / did not work: Animal gains modest; distant tumours only slowed
25. Went wrong / did not work: Clinic products contaminated or made non-sterile
26. What went wrong: No human trial, no human dose finding, no human drug levels. Mouse survival gains in AML were modest, not cures. Tumours at a distance from the injection site were slowed rather than cleared. Products sold to patients were contaminated or made in non-sterile conditions.
27. Most reported: Sold to patients via overseas clinics and online
28. Most reported: Nebulised, IV, suppository and Sub-Q forms
29. Most reported: Case of massive GI bleeding reported
30. Most reported: No documented human benefit

## What has been tested
31. Cancer biology: Pancreatic, breast, leukaemia, AML, colon, ovarian, cervical cancer cells (cell)
32. Cancer biology: Fresh ovarian cancer cells from 2 patients (ex vivo) (cell)
33. Cancer biology: AML mice and human AML grafts; colon tumour nodules; PNC-28 pancreatic tumours (animal)
34. Cell studies in pancreatic, breast, leukaemia (K562 and three AML lines), colon, ovarian (including cells taken fresh from two patients) and cervical cancer. Animal work: PNC-28 in mice with rat pancreatic tumours (2006); PNC-27 in mice with colon tumour nodules (2021); and an independent City of Hope and Zhejiang group testing PNC-27 in mouse and human-derived AML (2019). No human trial has ever been registered.
35. What it helps: All efficacy data are from cells, fresh tumour cells from two patients, and a few mouse studies. PNC-27 kills pancreatic, breast, leukaemia, colon, ovarian and cervical cancer cells while sparing matching normal cells. In mice, an independent AML study found longer survival but not cure. No human trial has been run or registered. It has been sold directly to cancer patients outside the US as inhaled, IV and suppository products, which the FDA warned against in 2017 after finding bacterial contamination; a US maker of kitchen-made suppositories pleaded guilty in 2021. The community record holds no documented benefit and one reported case of severe GI bleeding.
36. Trial: none. No PNC-27 or PNC-28 study registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (independent search reported 4 Aug 2026; direct registry query not possible here). The Pincus lab bio has said trials are coming since the 2000s, and its 2024 crowdfunding was suspended. (checked 2026-10-23) [S1]

## Who shouldn't take it
37. People with cancer using it instead of treatment: FDA warned cancer patients not to use PNC-27 products. (verified)

## Where it comes from
38. Designed in Matthew Pincus's lab at SUNY Downstate in Brooklyn. In 2001 the group fused short pieces of p53, the protein that normally guards cells against cancer, to a cell-entry sequence, hoping to restore p53 function. Instead the peptides killed cancer cells outright. The 12 to 26 version became PNC-27; a shorter 17 to 26 version became PNC-28.
39. First studied for: Killing cancer cells regardless of their p53 status, first breast cancer cells (2003), then pancreatic cancer in mice using PNC-28 (2006).
40. Name story: The peptide is a chimera: p53 residues 12 to 26, the bit that grips HDM-2, welded to a cell-entry tail related to penetratin from the fruit-fly Antennapedia gene, whose mutation grows legs where antennae should be. [S2] (verified)
41. 2001: PNAS: p53 12 to 26 fused to a cell-entry sequence kills cancer cells, even without p53
42. 2003: Oncogene: kills breast cancer cells by necrosis, not apoptosis
43. 2006: Sister peptide PNC-28 destroys pancreatic tumours in mice
44. 2010: PNAS: target found, HDM-2 sitting in the cancer-cell membrane
45. 2015: Kills ovarian cancer cells taken fresh from patients
46. Jan 2017: FDA warns patients after bacteria found in an inhaled product; second species found in March
47. Oct 2017: Case abstract: massive GI bleeding during experimental use
48. 2019: Independent group: lengthens survival in AML mice and cuts leukaemia stem cells
49. 2020–2021: Alabama man indicted, then pleads guilty, over kitchen-made PNC-27 suppositories sold to patients and a Mexican clinic
50. 2021: Colon tumour nodules die in mice
51. 2022–2024: Pore structure imaged; mitochondrial damage added; lab crowdfunding suspended
52. 2025: Kills cervical cancer cells; ketone salts boost the effect
53. Oct 2026: Still preclinical, no registered trial; sold online as a research peptide

# Semax + Selank + PE-22-28 + Pinealon
Page: https://baresignals.co/library/#/p/illumineuro
Checked against Library v68, exported 2026-10-25

## Identity
1. Also called: IllumiNeuro, IllumiNeuro Protocol, Illumineuro 46 mg, Illumineuro 48 mg, NA Selank + NA Semax + PE-22-28 + Pinealon
2. Origin: Blend of 4 peptides
3. Legal and approval status: US: not approved. Semax won an 8-5-1 PCAC vote in July 2026 (plain Semax, not the NA amidate); Selank, PE-22-28 and Pinealon have no US status. Russia: plain Semax and Selank approved; the NA forms and the blend are not. WADA: S0.

## Summary
4. IllumiNeuro is a four-peptide brain blend combining N-acetyl Semax amidate, N-acetyl Selank amidate, PE-22-28 (a spadin fragment) and Pinealon. People use it for focus, mood and brain support, combining Semax for BDNF and drive, Selank for calm, PE-22-28 for mood and Pinealon for brain protection. The blend itself has never been studied, and the N-acetyl amidate forms have no published human data.
5. Punch line: Four-peptide brain stack: Semax for focus, Selank for calm, PE-22-28 for mood, Pinealon for protection and sleep.
6. Used for: Focus, mood, brain support

## Roles (what it is used for, strongest first)
7. Cognition: NA Semax for focus and BDNF
8. Mood: PE-22-28 antidepressant in mice; Selank calm
9. Neural protection: Pinealon and Semax brain protection
10. Neural plasticity: PE-22-28 neurite outgrowth, Semax BDNF
11. Sleep & rhythms (backed only by animal or user reports): Pinealon circadian, vivid dreams
12. Drive & mental stamina (backed only by animal or user reports): Semax activating

## How it works
13. Raises brain growth factor · BDNF and TrkB up (Semax) · role Cognition
   Semax raises levels of BDNF, a growth factor for nerve cells, and of TrkB, the receptor it binds. More BDNF signalling favours new synapses and nerve cell survival. This is shown in animals for plain Semax; the capped NA amidate form has not been studied for it.
14. Calms anxiety · Enkephalinase inhibition, GABA-linked (Selank) · role Mood
   Selank slows enkephalinase, the enzymes that break down the body's own calming enkephalin peptides, and is linked to GABA signalling. The aim is calm without heavy sedation. Russian clinical data cover plain Selank in anxiety; the NA amidate version in this blend has no trial data.
15. Lifts mood in mice · TREK-1 channel block (PE-22-28) · role Mood
   PE-22-28, a short piece of spadin, blocks TREK-1, a potassium channel that keeps neurons quiet. With that brake eased, serotonin neurons fire more readily. Antidepressant-like effects and better stability than spadin are shown in mouse tests only.
16. Protects brain cells under stress · Pinealon, oxidative stress models · role Neural protection
   Pinealon is a three amino acid Khavinson bioregulator tested on neurons under oxidative stress, the damage caused by reactive oxygen. In those models it limited cell injury. The evidence comes from cell and animal work by one research group, with no human trials.
17. Mechanism overview: N-acetyl Semax amidate and N-acetyl Selank amidate are Semax (MEHFPGP) and Selank (TKPRPGP) capped at both ends, sold as longer-lasting. PE-22-28 (GVSWGLR) is the shortest active fragment of spadin and blocks the TREK-1 potassium channel, with antidepressant effects and better stability than spadin in mice. Pinealon (Glu-Asp-Arg) is a Khavinson bioregulator studied for neuron protection against oxidative stress. The blend stacks focus, calm, mood and protection signals.

## What is inside the blend
18. NA Semax Amidate: 20 mg · Focus, alertness, BDNF
19. PE-22-28: 10 mg · Mood via TREK-1 block
20. Pinealon: 10 mg · Neuron protection, circadian
21. NA Selank Amidate: 6 mg · Calm, anxiety relief
22. Most common ratio: NA Semax 20 · NA Selank 10 · Pinealon 10 · PE-22-28 10 = 50 mg (2 of 7 listings state it (+1 sells 50 mg unsplit); 50 mg total on 4 of 7)
23. Other ratio seen: NA Semax 20 · PE-22-28 10 · Pinealon 10 · NA Selank 8 = 48 mg (2 listings)
24. Other ratio seen: NA Semax 20 · PE-22-28 10 · Pinealon 10 · NA Selank 6 = 46 mg (1 listing)
25. Other ratio seen: NA Semax 22 · NA Selank 9 · PE-22-28 10 · Pinealon 10 = 50 mg label (sums 51) (1 listing)
26. Other ratio seen: Semax 10 · Selank 10 · Pinealon 20 · PE-22-28 10 = 50 mg (1 listing)
27. Version Common retail: NA Semax 20 · PE-22-28 10 · Pinealon 10 · NA Selank 6 = 46 mg
28. Why NA Semax Amidate is in it: The focus and drive engine
29. Why NA Selank Amidate is in it: Calm, to offset Semax
30. Why PE-22-28 is in it: A mood lane none of the others hit (TREK-1)
31. Why Pinealon is in it: Protection and sleep-rhythm signal
32. Mixing chemistry: Semax brings Met and His and PE-22-28 a Trp: oxidation is the watch point; keep cold and dark.
33. Mixing chemistry: Pinealon (Glu-Asp-Arg) and Selank are chemically quiet.
34. Mixing chemistry: All four are short (3 to 7 residues), so clumping risk is low.
35. Mixing chemistry: Often sprayed nasally, where the liquid's formulation is not disclosed.
36. Self-mixing: Separate vials let you drop PE-22-28 or Pinealon and titrate Semax on its own; four vials and four ratios is the trade-off.

## Dosage (community reported unless tagged)
37. Typical: 100–500 mcg total blend · 1× daily, morning · cycle 4–8 weeks · route Sub-Q, nasal (reported)
38. Half-life: per component
39. Most people take: 100 to 500 mcg of total blend a day. The listed 2 mL mix (24 mg/mL) puts that at 0.4 to 2 units, too small to draw accurately; 5 mL gives about 1 to 5 units, 10 mL about 2 to 10.

## What people report
40. Sub-Q once daily in the morning, 100 to 500 mcg of total blend, 4 to 8 weeks. Some use it intranasally.
41. Liked / worked: Each part aims at a different brain lane
42. Liked / worked: PE-22-28 beat spadin in mouse tests
43. Liked / worked: Plain Semax and Selank have Russian clinical use
44. What worked: No public user report pool found for the blend. Aggregator pages list it with a 100 to 500 mcg daily dose and describe it by component mechanism only.
45. Went wrong / did not work: No study of the blend
46. Went wrong / did not work: NA forms have no human data
47. Went wrong / did not work: Two published ratios, 46 and 48 mg
48. What went wrong: Common side effects listed: injection-site reactions, nasal irritation if sprayed, vivid dreams (put down to Pinealon), early headache. Caution listed for bipolar disorder, psychosis and seizure disorders. The N-acetyl amidate forms have no published human data at all.
49. Most reported: 100 to 500 mcg total, mornings
50. Most reported: Run 4 to 8 weeks
51. Most reported: Some spray it nasally

## What has been tested
52. Never tested as a combination; the product's own page says there are no clinical studies on this four-peptide mix. Components: PE-22-28 in mice (Djillani 2017); Pinealon in Khavinson cell and animal work; Semax and Selank in Russian clinical use (as the non-acetylated forms).
53. What it helps: No study of the blend. PE-22-28: mouse antidepressant tests. Pinealon: cell and animal work. Semax and Selank: Russian clinical data for the plain forms, none for the NA amidates. User reports for the blend are not public.

## Who shouldn't take it
54. People with a history of seizures: Russian prescribing info for Semax lists convulsive disorders as a contraindication. (inferred)
55. People on benzodiazepines or other sedatives: Selank modulates GABA-A receptors; effects may stack. (inferred)
56. People with active or recent cancer: Marketed as gene-regulating and proliferative; effect on tumours untested. (inferred)
57. People with acute psychosis or severe anxiety: Raises dopamine and serotonin turnover. (inferred)

## Synergies (paired with)
58. Semax + Selank: Semax + Selank is the two-peptide core of this blend in plain form, without PE-22-28 and Pinealon. People choose it to keep the focus and calm pair alone. Stacking both duplicates the same peptides and has not been tested.
59. Cerebrolysin: Cerebrolysin adds a pig brain peptide mix with nerve growth factor-like activity and dementia and stroke trial data, alongside this blend's BDNF, calm and mood signals. The pairing is user logic, not trial data.
60. Dihexa: Dihexa works through a different growth signal, HGF and its receptor c-Met, while Semax here works through BDNF. People pair them for memory from two angles. Dihexa has rat data only, and the pair has not been tested together.
61. Epitalon: Epitalon is another Khavinson peptide, used for sleep rhythm and longevity, which overlaps with Pinealon's pineal signal here. Its own claims are unverified, and the pairing is user logic, not trial data.

## Where it comes from
62. A four-peptide brain blend: N-acetyl Semax amidate, N-acetyl Selank amidate, PE-22-28 (a spadin fragment) and Pinealon (Glu-Asp-Arg).
63. First studied for: Marketed as a cognitive and mood blend: Semax for focus, Selank for calm, PE-22-28 for mood via TREK-1, Pinealon for brain and circadian support.
64. Name story: A product name: illuminate plus neuro. Not a scientific term. [S1] (inferred)
65. 1990s to 2000s: Semax and Selank approved in Russia
66. 2000s: Pinealon (EDR) developed in Khavinson's group
67. 2017: PE-22-28 shown to work in mice as a shortened spadin
68. 2020s: NA amidate versions of Semax and Selank sold
69. 2026: IllumiNeuro sold at 46 and 48 mg
70. Today: Sold as a nootropic blend, Sub-Q or nasal

# Bimagrumab
Page: https://baresignals.co/library/#/p/bimagrumab
Checked against Library v68, exported 2026-10-25

## Identity
1. Also called: BYM338, LY3985863
2. Origin: Lab-designed antibody
3. Legal and approval status: Phase 2 as of Oct 2026: BELIEVE published in Nature Medicine 2026, a tirzepatide combo Phase 2 (NCT06643728) ongoing, a diabetes combo trial stopped Sep 2025; no Phase 3 announced. WADA bans anti-activin receptor IIB antibodies under S4 (reported).

## Summary
4. Bimagrumab is a Novartis antibody that blocks activin type II receptors, cutting off the myostatin and activin signals that cap muscle growth. Built for muscle-wasting disease, it is now studied for fat loss that spares muscle. A Phase 2 in type 2 diabetes removed about a fifth of fat mass while adding lean mass. It failed in inclusion body myositis, and cramps, acne and dropouts are concerns.
5. Punch line: Antibody that lifts the myostatin brake on muscle. Weight drops as fat while lean mass holds or grows.
6. Used for: Fat loss while keeping muscle

## Roles (what it is used for, strongest first)
7. Muscle & performance: Builds and keeps lean mass
8. Fat metabolism: Burns fat, spares muscle
9. Glucose & insulin: Better HbA1c and insulin sensitivity
10. Inflammatory signaling: hsCRP down up to 84%
11. Aging & senescence (backed only by animal or user reports): Tested for age-related muscle loss

## How it works
12. Blocks the brake on muscle growth · ActRIIA/ActRIIB antagonist · role Muscle & performance
   Bimagrumab is an antibody that blocks activin type II receptors A and B (ActRIIA and ActRIIB). These receptors carry the signals that hold muscle size in check. Blocking them lets muscle fibres grow, shown in human phase 2 trials.
13. Shuts out myostatin and activin signals · Myostatin, activin A, GDF-11 · role Muscle & performance
   Myostatin, activin A and GDF-11 all signal through these receptors to limit muscle growth. With the receptors blocked, none of them can act, which removes several brakes at once. Lean mass rose in human trials, though it failed to help inclusion body myositis.
14. Pushes fat toward burning · Adipose ActRII blockade, browning · role Fat metabolism
   The same receptors sit on fat cells. Blocking them there shifts fat toward breakdown and burning, with signs of browning. In a 2021 phase 2 trial in type 2 diabetes, monthly infusions removed about a fifth of fat mass.
15. Improves insulin sensitivity · Muscle and fat glucose uptake · role Glucose & insulin
   With more muscle and less fat, glucose uptake into muscle and fat improves and the body responds better to insulin. The 2021 phase 2 in type 2 diabetes showed HbA1c falling alongside fat loss.
16. Mechanism overview: Bimagrumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody that binds activin type II receptors A and B (ActRIIA/ActRIIB). These receptors carry the signals of myostatin, activin A and GDF-11, which normally hold muscle size in check, so blocking them lifts the brake and muscle fibres grow. The same receptors sit on fat cells, and blocking them there shifts fat toward breakdown and oxidation and improves insulin sensitivity. The result is a drug that removes fat and adds lean mass at the same time, unlike GLP-1 drugs, which cut appetite and lose some muscle along the way.

## Dosage (community reported unless tagged)
17. Typical: 10 or 30 mg/kg · every 4 or 12 weeks · cycle 48–72 weeks in trials · route IV (Sub-Q version in trials) (verified)
18. Half-life: Long (weeks); allows monthly or quarterly IV
19. Dose note: Weight-based IV dosing from trials only; Sub-Q dose not published.
20. Most people take: Trial doses only, by IV infusion: 10 mg/kg every 4 weeks (2021 diabetes trial) or 10 or 30 mg/kg every 12 weeks with loading doses (BELIEVE). A weekly Sub-Q form is in Phase 2. No community dose.
21. Monthly IV: 10 mg/kg (max 1,200 mg) · every 4 weeks · 48 weeks · IV · for 2021 Phase 2, type 2 diabetes with obesity [S1] (verified)
22. Quarterly IV: 10 or 30 mg/kg · every 12 weeks, extra doses at wk 1 and 4 · 48–72 weeks · IV · for BELIEVE, with or without semaglutide [S2] (verified)

## What people report
23. Essentially no grey-market use, since an IV antibody is hard to copy; discussion is about trial data and whether it will rescue muscle on GLP-1s.
24. Liked / worked: Fat mass -20.5%, lean +3.6% in T2D
25. Liked / worked: 22.1% weight loss with semaglutide
26. Liked / worked: About 92% of loss was fat
27. Liked / worked: HbA1c down 0.76 points
28. Liked / worked: hsCRP down up to 84%
29. What worked: In type 2 diabetes it cut fat mass 20.5% while adding 3.6% lean mass over 48 weeks; in BELIEVE the high-dose combo with semaglutide gave 22.1% weight loss at 72 weeks, about 92% of it fat.
30. Went wrong / did not work: Failed in inclusion body myositis
31. Went wrong / did not work: Muscle spasms and cramps
32. Went wrong / did not work: Diarrhea and acne
33. Went wrong / did not work: Lipase, liver enzyme and CK rises
34. Went wrong / did not work: 14–21% quit for side effects
35. What went wrong: Failed to improve walking in inclusion body myositis; muscle spasms, diarrhea and acne; rises in lipase, liver enzymes and CK; 14–21% quit bimagrumab arms for side effects.
36. Most reported: No grey-market supply
37. Most reported: Analysts wary of dropout rates
38. Most reported: Hope for muscle-sparing GLP-1 regimens

## What has been tested
39. Fat metabolism: Obesity with type 2 diabetes, Phase 2 (human)
40. Fat metabolism: Obesity with semaglutide, BELIEVE (human)
41. Muscle & performance: Inclusion body myositis, Phase 2b/3 (human)
42. Aging & senescence: Sarcopenia in older adults, Phase 2 (human)
43. Glucose & insulin: HbA1c in type 2 diabetes (human)
44. Phase 2/3 in inclusion body myositis (failed 2016), Phase 2 in sarcopenia, a 2021 Phase 2 in type 2 diabetes with obesity, and Phase 2b BELIEVE (507 people) with semaglutide.
45. What it helps: In a 2021 Phase 2 in type 2 diabetes, monthly infusions removed about a fifth of fat mass while adding lean mass and lowering HbA1c. BELIEVE showed that pairing it with semaglutide pushed weight loss to about 22% with most of it fat, and bimagrumab alone raised lean mass. It failed in inclusion body myositis. Interest is in muscle-sparing GLP-1 therapy; muscle cramps, acne, diarrhea, enzyme rises and a high dropout rate are the concerns.
46. Trial: active · Phase 2 · obesity with tirzepatide · NCT06643728 · Eli Lilly. Lilly's muscle sparing antibody finished dosing in January 2026 with results expected in 2026, after a planned Phase 2b was withdrawn in 2025. (checked 2026-10-23) [S3] (verified)

## Who shouldn't take it
47. People planning conception: Activin blockade alters FSH; class drug sotatercept impairs fertility. (inferred)
48. People on blood thinners or bleeding disorders: Class drug sotatercept causes bleeding and telangiectasia. (inferred)

## Synergies (paired with)
49. Semaglutide: Semaglutide cuts appetite through the GLP-1 receptor but loses some muscle along with fat, while bimagrumab adds lean mass and removes fat. In the BELIEVE trial, the pair reached about 22% weight loss, mostly fat.
50. Tirzepatide: Tirzepatide drives large weight loss through GIP and GLP-1 receptors, with some muscle lost along the way. Bimagrumab is added to protect lean mass. BELIEVE tested it with semaglutide; this pair has not been tested.

## Where it comes from
51. A Novartis antibody (BYM338) that blocks activin type II receptors, cutting off the myostatin and activin signals that cap muscle growth; built for muscle-wasting disease, reborn as a fat-loss drug.
52. First studied for: Muscle wasting: sporadic inclusion body myositis, sarcopenia and hip-fracture recovery.
53. Name story: Started life as Novartis code BYM338, made with MorphoSys antibody technology; the '-umab' ending marks a fully human monoclonal antibody. Lilly renamed its programme LY3985863. [S4] (reported)
54. 2013: FDA breakthrough status for inclusion body myositis
55. 2016: Phase 2b/3 in inclusion body myositis fails
56. 2021: Phase 2 in type 2 diabetes: fat down 20%, muscle up
57. Jul 2023: Lilly buys Versanis for up to $1.9B
58. Sep 2025: Lilly stops tirzepatide combo trial in diabetes
59. 2026: BELIEVE published: 22% loss with semaglutide; tirzepatide trial ongoing

# UBT-251
Page: https://baresignals.co/library/#/p/ubt-251
Checked against Library v68, exported 2026-10-25

## Identity
1. Also called: UBT251, triple G agonist, GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist
2. Origin: Lab-designed
3. Legal and approval status: Investigational as of Oct 2026. China: phase 3 started Sep 2026 (obesity, 600 people; T2D UNIGUIDE-1 and -2). Global (Novo): phase 1b/2a in obesity, data 2027; global T2D phase 2 planned 2H 2026. Not on the WADA list by name.

## Summary
4. UBT-251 is a triple agonist of GLP-1, GIP and glucagon receptors from United Biotechnology in China, the same class as retatrutide. It is developed for obesity and type 2 diabetes, and Novo Nordisk licensed rights outside Greater China in March 2025. Chinese phase 2 trials cut weight up to 19.7% in 24 weeks. Data are short and limited to Chinese adults, and nobody outside trials uses it.
5. Punch line: China's retatrutide rival, a GLP-1, GIP, glucagon triple. Novo licensed it; up to 19.7% lost in 24 weeks.
6. Used for: Obesity, type 2 diabetes

## Roles (what it is used for, strongest first)
7. Fat metabolism: Up to 19.7% loss in 24 wk
8. Glucose & insulin: HbA1c down up to 2.16 points
9. Appetite & satiety: GLP-1/GIP hunger suppression
10. Heart & vessels: Lower blood pressure and lipids
11. Organ function (backed only by animal or user reports): Liver and kidney trials cleared

## How it works
12. Quiets hunger, slows stomach · GLP-1 receptor · role Appetite & satiety
   GLP-1 receptor activation in the brain's appetite centres cuts hunger, and in the gut it slows stomach emptying. People eat less and feel full longer. This is the core of the weight loss seen in the Chinese Phase 2 human trials.
13. Boosts insulin response, may ease nausea · GIP receptor · role Glucose & insulin
   GIP receptor activation on pancreatic beta cells adds to insulin release when glucose is high. GIP signalling is also thought to soften the nausea GLP-1 drugs cause, though that has not been shown for this drug specifically. In the diabetes trial, HbA1c fell more than on semaglutide.
14. Raises energy use and liver fat burning · Glucagon receptor · role Fat metabolism
   Glucagon receptor activation raises energy use and pushes the liver to burn its stored fat. This is why triple agonists are also aimed at fatty liver. Glucagon can raise blood sugar, which the GLP-1 and GIP arms offset.
15. Weekly dosing · Long-acting modification (undisclosed) · role Fat metabolism
   A long-acting chemical modification, not publicly disclosed, keeps the peptide in the body for about a week. That allows once-weekly injections. The exact design is unpublished.
16. Mechanism overview: UBT251 is a long-acting synthetic peptide that activates three receptors. GLP-1 receptor agonism cuts appetite, slows gastric emptying and raises glucose-dependent insulin. GIP receptor agonism adds insulin secretion and may soften GLP-1 nausea. Glucagon receptor agonism raises energy expenditure and drives fat burning in the liver, which is why triple agonists are also aimed at fatty liver; it can push glucose up, which the other two arms offset.

## Dosage (community reported unless tagged)
17. Typical: 2–6 mg · once weekly · cycle Trial only (24 wk) · route Sub-Q (verified)
18. Half-life: Long-acting, weekly (not published)
19. Dose note: Titration steps for the 2 and 6 mg arms not published. Outliyr lists no protocol.
20. Most people take: Trial only: 2, 4 or 6 mg weekly Sub-Q for 24 weeks; one 4 mg arm started at 0.5 mg and another at 1 mg. No community protocol exists.
21. Phase 2 obesity: 2–6 mg · 1× weekly · 24 wk; 0.5 or 1 mg start in 4 mg arms · Sub-Q · for Chinese adults with obesity [S1] [S2] (verified)
22. Phase 2 T2D: 2–6 mg · 1× weekly · 24 wk · Sub-Q · for Chinese adults with T2D [S3] (verified)

## What people report
23. Essentially no grey-market or community reports found as of Oct 2026.
24. Liked / worked: Up to 19.7% loss in 24 weeks
25. Liked / worked: 48% lost at least 20%
26. Liked / worked: HbA1c down 2.16 vs 1.77 on semaglutide
27. Liked / worked: No plateau at 24 weeks
28. What worked: Up to 19.7% weight loss in 24 weeks versus 2.0% on placebo, with no plateau; 48% lost at least 20%. In diabetes, HbA1c fell up to 2.16 points versus 1.77 on semaglutide 1 mg, with 9.8% weight loss.
29. Went wrong / did not work: GI side effects, mostly mild to moderate
30. Went wrong / did not work: Adverse event rates not yet published
31. Went wrong / did not work: Only Chinese data, short trials
32. What went wrong: GI side effects, mostly mild to moderate and easing over time; detailed rates not released. Data so far is short (24 weeks) and only from Chinese adults with lower baseline weight.
33. Most reported: No community reports found

## What has been tested
34. Fat metabolism: Obesity, phase 1b and phase 2 (China) (human)
35. Glucose & insulin: Type 2 diabetes, phase 2 vs semaglutide (human)
36. Heart & vessels: Blood pressure and lipids (secondary) (human)
37. Phase 1b in China (36 people, 12 weeks), two Chinese phase 2 trials in obesity (205) and type 2 diabetes (211), then Chinese phase 3 from Sep 2026; Novo runs a global phase 1b/2a.
38. What it helps: In Chinese phase 2 trials it cut weight up to 19.7% in 24 weeks without a plateau, and in diabetes lowered HbA1c more than semaglutide 1 mg with twice the weight loss. Blood pressure, waist and lipids improved. Side effects were mostly GI. It is a retatrutide-class drug with far less data, and nobody outside trials is using it.
39. Trial: active · Phase 2 · obesity · Novo Nordisk. After 19.7 percent weight loss in a Chinese Phase 2, Novo is running a global Phase 1b/2a with data due 2027. (checked 2026-10-23) [S4] (reported)

## Who shouldn't take it
40. Personal or family history of MTC or MEN2: Causes thyroid C-cell tumours in rodents; boxed warning and contraindication on the label. (inferred)
41. Anyone booked for surgery, endoscopy or sedation: Food can stay in the stomach for days and be inhaled into the lungs under anaesthesia. (inferred)
42. People with arrhythmia or a fast resting pulse: The glucagon part of the drug pushes resting heart rate up. (inferred)

## Synergies (paired with)
43. Retatrutide: Retatrutide hits the same three receptors, GLP-1, GIP and glucagon, so the two are alternatives in the same class. Retatrutide has far more data. Stacking two triple agonists has no logic behind it and has not been tested.
44. Semaglutide: Semaglutide works only on GLP-1, while UBT-251 adds GIP and glucagon arms. It was the comparator in the diabetes trial, where UBT-251 lowered HbA1c more. They are alternatives, not a tested combination.

## Where it comes from
45. A triple agonist of GLP-1, GIP and glucagon receptors from The United Laboratories' subsidiary United Biotechnology in China, the same class as retatrutide. Novo Nordisk licensed rights outside Greater China in March 2025.
46. First studied for: Obesity and type 2 diabetes; China also cleared trials in fatty liver and chronic kidney disease.
47. Name story: UBT is United Biotechnology, the TUL subsidiary that discovered it, and 251 is its compound number. No INN has been published as of Oct 2026. [S5] (inferred)
48. 2024: Chinese phase 1b: 15.1% loss in 12 weeks at top dose
49. Mar 2025: Novo licenses ex-China rights ($200M upfront, up to $1.8B milestones)
50. Feb 2026: China phase 2 obesity: up to 19.7% in 24 weeks
51. Mar 2026: China phase 2 T2D: beats semaglutide 1 mg on HbA1c and weight
52. Sep 2026: First patients dosed in Chinese phase 3 (obesity and T2D)
53. Today: Global Novo data due 2027

# SLU-PP-332 + BAM-15 oral
Page: https://baresignals.co/library/#/p/slu-pp-332-bam-15
Checked against Library v68, exported 2026-10-25

## Identity
1. Also called: SLU-PP-332 / BAM15 capsules, SLUBAM, BAM15 + SLU-PP-332 stack, ERR agonist + mitochondrial uncoupler, oral fat-loss stack
2. Origin: Blend of 2 small molecules, oral capsule
3. Legal and approval status: Preclinical everywhere: no approved product, no registered human trial for either compound. Sold as a research chemical. WADA: SLU-PP-332 is an ERR agonist, and metabolic modulators are banned under S4 (inferred); BAM-15 falls under S0.

## Summary
4. This oral capsule pairs two lab compounds sold for fat loss: BAM-15, a mitochondrial uncoupler that makes cells burn fuel as heat, and SLU-PP-332, an exercise mimic that switches on ERR receptors. All evidence is in mice and per compound, and neither has a human trial. The capsule's SLU-PP-332 share is tiny and poorly absorbed, so it works, if at all, as a BAM-15 tablet.
5. Punch line: Oral fat-loss capsule: an exercise mimic plus a mitochondrial uncoupler that burns fuel as heat. Mouse data only.
6. Used for: Fat loss, often on top of a GLP-1

## Roles (what it is used for, strongest first)
7. Cellular energy: BAM-15 burns fuel as heat; SLU-PP-332 mimics exercise
8. Fat metabolism: Both cut fat mass in mice
9. Muscle & performance: SLU-PP-332 raised endurance in mice
10. Glucose & insulin: BAM-15 improved insulin response in mice
11. Organ function (backed only by animal or user reports): BAM-15 cleared liver fat in mice

## How it works
12. Lets mitochondria leak protons so fuel burns as heat · Mitochondrial uncoupling, inner membrane · role Cellular energy
   BAM-15 carries protons back across the inner mitochondrial membrane, uncoupling fuel burning from ATP production. The cell has to burn more fat and sugar to keep its energy up, and the extra is lost as heat. Unlike DNP, it spares the outer cell membrane. Shown in mice.
13. Cut fat and liver fat without eating less · BAM15 in diet-induced obese mice · role Fat metabolism
   In diet-induced obese mice, BAM-15 taken in food cut body fat and liver fat and improved insulin response on clamp testing. Food intake, lean mass and body temperature did not change. These are mouse results; there are no human studies.
14. Switches on the 'exercise' genes in muscle · ERRα/β/γ agonist · role Muscle & performance
   SLU-PP-332 switches on ERR alpha, beta and gamma, the estrogen-related receptors that run endurance gene programmes in muscle. That builds more mitochondria and shifts muscle toward fat burning. Shown in mice given injections; it is described as poorly absorbed by mouth.
15. More fat burning and endurance in mice · Oxidative fibre shift, PGC-1α · role Cellular energy
   Through PGC-1α and an oxidative fibre shift, injected SLU-PP-332 raised treadmill endurance and cut fat mass in mice. The oral dose in this capsule is far below any studied amount. Nobody has tested the two compounds together.
16. Mechanism overview: BAM-15 is a lipophilic weak acid that carries protons across the mitochondrial inner membrane, uncoupling oxidation from ATP synthesis without depolarising the plasma membrane (unlike DNP). In diet-induced obese mice it was orally bioavailable and reduced fat mass and hepatic lipids, improving insulin sensitivity on clamp, with no change in food intake, lean mass or body temperature. SLU-PP-332 is a synthetic pan-agonist of estrogen-related receptors α, β and γ that drives oxidative muscle gene programmes; mice received 25 to 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally once or twice daily. Its oral bioavailability is described as poor, which led to the orally active analogue SLU-PP-915. A 250 mcg oral dose is roughly 0.1% of a mouse-scaled 50 mg/kg dose.

## What is inside the blend
17. BAM-15 50 mg: 50 mg per capsule · Uncoupler: raises resting fuel burn, works by mouth
18. SLU-PP-332 250 mcg: 0.25 mg per capsule · ERR agonist: exercise-like muscle signal (tiny oral share)
19. Most common ratio: BAM-15 50 mg · SLU-PP-332 250 mcg per capsule, 60 capsules = 50.25 mg per capsule (9 of 10 listings)
20. Other ratio seen: BAM-15 50 mg · SLU-PP-332 50 mg per capsule = 100 mg per capsule (1 listing (option))
21. Other ratio seen: BAM-15 50 mg · SLU-PP-332 100 mcg per vial = liquid vial (1 listing, discontinued)
22. Version Most listings: BAM-15 50 mg · SLU-PP-332 250 mcg per capsule, 60 capsules = 50.25 mg per capsule
23. Version Older tablet (not found this pass): SLU-PP-332 100 mcg · BAM-15 25 mg per tablet, 60 tablets = 25.1 mg per tablet
24. Why BAM-15 is in it: The only part with oral fat-loss data; raises calorie burn at rest
25. Why SLU-PP-332 is in it: Adds an exercise-like muscle signal, in theory
26. Mixing chemistry: Dry capsule, not a liquid vial: no pH or reconstitution issues.
27. Mixing chemistry: Main risk is fill accuracy: 250 mcg is hard to spread evenly through a 50 mg capsule.
28. Mixing chemistry: Keep dry and sealed; moisture and heat speed breakdown of both.
29. Mixing chemistry: Ask for per-component mg by LC-MS or HPLC, not one purity number.
30. Self-mixing: Buying each as separate capsules lets people dose BAM-15 and SLU-PP-332 independently; the combined capsule locks a ratio that is almost all BAM-15.

## Dosage (community reported unless tagged)
31. Typical: 1 capsule (50 mg BAM-15, 250 mcg SLU-PP-332) · 1× daily · cycle 4–8 weeks (BAM-15 reports) · route Oral (reported)
32. Half-life: per component
33. Most people take: No standard dose. People size it by the BAM-15 share: one 50 mg capsule a day; guides cap BAM-15 near 70 mg a day, so a second capsule goes past it. The SLU-PP-332 that comes along is far below any studied amount.

## What people report
34. One capsule a day; seller guides cap BAM-15 near 70 mg a day. People watch for warmth, sweating and a fast heartbeat. An older tablet used 25 mg BAM-15 with 100 mcg SLU-PP-332. Often stacked with a GLP-1 such as retatrutide.
35. Liked / worked: BAM-15 cut fat without eating less, in mice
36. Liked / worked: BAM-15 works by mouth in mice
37. Liked / worked: SLU-PP-332 raised endurance in mice
38. What worked: In mice, each one lowered fat and improved insulin response. Seller content claims the pair burns fat 'at rest and in training' while keeping muscle; no human outcome data back it.
39. Went wrong / did not work: Never given to people in a trial
40. Went wrong / did not work: SLU-PP-332 share ~1/800 of the mouse-scaled dose
41. Went wrong / did not work: Uncoupler class carries overheating risk
42. What went wrong: The SLU-PP-332 share is tiny. 250 mcg is roughly 1/800 of the dose used in mice after scaling to a human, and the compound is poorly absorbed orally, so the capsule works, if at all, as a BAM-15 tablet. One reviewer reported fatigue and burnout within two weeks on SLU-PP-332 alone.
43. Most reported: One capsule a day
44. Most reported: Warmth, sweating, fast heartbeat
45. Most reported: Cap near 70 mg BAM-15 a day
46. Most reported: Stacked with GLP-1s

## What has been tested
47. Fat metabolism: BAM15 in diet-induced obese mice, oral (mouse)
48. Glucose & insulin: BAM15 clamp studies (mouse)
49. Muscle & performance: SLU-PP-332 treadmill endurance, injected (mouse)
50. Fat metabolism: The two combined (none)
51. Never tested together. BAM-15: orally bioavailable in mice, cut body fat and liver fat without changing food intake, lean mass or body temperature (Nature Communications 2020). SLU-PP-332: given by injection to mice at 25 to 50 mg/kg; raised endurance and cut fat mass; described as poorly absorbed by mouth.
52. What it helps: All evidence is in mice and per compound. BAM-15 cut body fat and liver fat and improved insulin response when eaten in food. SLU-PP-332 improved endurance and fat mass when injected. Nobody has tested the pair, and the capsule's SLU-PP-332 share is far below any studied amount.

## Who shouldn't take it
53. People exercising or living in heat: Uncouplers like DNP cause fatal overheating. (inferred)
54. Drug-tested athletes: Sold as an "exercise mimetic"; metabolic modulators fall under WADA S4.4. (inferred)
55. People on thyroid hormone or stimulants: Metabolic rate already raised; heat load stacks. (inferred)
56. People with heart disease: ERR agonism reshapes heart muscle metabolism; no human data at all. (inferred)

## Synergies (paired with)
57. Retatrutide: Retatrutide cuts appetite and raises energy use through three receptors, with large human trials. This capsule adds a calorie burn signal without eating less, from mice only. The pairing is user logic, not trial data.
58. Tirzepatide: Tirzepatide cuts appetite through GIP and GLP-1 receptors and has large human trials. People add this capsule to raise calorie burn on top of eating less. The pair has not been tested together.
59. Semaglutide: Semaglutide reduces appetite through the GLP-1 receptor, while BAM-15 raised fat burning in mice without changing intake. People combine eating less with burning more. The pairing is user logic, not trial data.
60. MOTS-c: MOTS-c activates AMPK, the energy sensor, another exercise mimic route alongside SLU-PP-332's ERR signal. People stack them for endurance and fat loss. Each has mouse data only, and the pair has not been tested.
61. 5-Amino-1MQ: 5-Amino-1MQ blocks NNMT in fat cells and shrank fat cells in obese mice, a different target from uncoupling and ERR. People add it for fat loss. The pairing is user logic, not trial data.
62. L-Carnitine: L-carnitine shuttles fatty acids into mitochondria, feeding the fat burning that BAM-15 speeds up. The pairing makes sense on paper. Carnitine has small oral weight loss effects; the pair has not been tested.
63. AOD-9604: AOD-9604 is a growth hormone fragment aimed at fat breakdown, with rodent data only. Users add it to this capsule for fat loss. The pair has not been tested together.

## Where it comes from
64. An oral capsule pairing two lab compounds sold for fat loss: BAM-15, a mitochondrial uncoupler that makes cells burn fuel as heat, and SLU-PP-332, an 'exercise in a pill' that switches on ERR receptors. The common capsule holds 50 mg BAM-15 and 250 mcg SLU-PP-332, 60 capsules a bottle.
65. First studied for: Grey-market stack that took off in 2025, pitched as fat burning that spares muscle. Neither compound has been given to people in a registered trial.
66. Name story: SLU stands for Saint Louis University, where the ERR agonist series was made; PP-332 is its compound number. BAM15 is a code from its discovery screen. The name just lists both. [S1] (reported)
67. 2013: BAM15 described as a mitochondrial uncoupler that spares the cell membrane
68. 2020: BAM15 cuts fat and liver fat in obese mice, taken by mouth
69. 2023: SLU-PP-332 raises running endurance in mice
70. 2024: SLU-PP-332 eases metabolic syndrome in obese mice
71. 2025: Sold together as oral tablets and capsules
72. 2026: Oral successor SLU-PP-915 reported in mice

# Efocipegtrutide
Page: https://baresignals.co/library/#/p/efocipegtrutide
Checked against Library v68, exported 2026-10-25

## Identity
1. Also called: HM15211, LAPS Triple Agonist, LAPS GLP/GIP/GCG
2. Origin: Lab-modified natural chain: triple agonist peptide linked to an antibody Fc fragment
3. Legal and approval status: Investigational, not approved anywhere: global Phase 2b in MASH completed July 2026 with data under analysis as of Oct 2026; FDA Fast Track for MASH, FDA/EMA orphan designations for PSC, PBC and IPF. As an unapproved drug it falls under WADA S0 (inferred).

## Summary
4. Efocipegtrutide is Hanmi's weekly glucagon, GIP and GLP-1 triple agonist attached to an antibody Fc fragment so it lasts a week. It is aimed at fatty liver disease with fibrosis rather than maximum weight loss, with the glucagon arm burning fat inside the liver. A 12-week early trial cut liver fat up to 81% against 6% on placebo. The larger MASH trial is unreported, and community use is negligible.
5. Punch line: Liver-first weekly triple agonist, Fc-tagged to last. Liver fat fell up to 81% in 12 weeks.
6. Used for: MASH, liver fibrosis

## Roles (what it is used for, strongest first)
7. Organ function: Clears liver fat, targets fibrosis
8. Inflammatory signaling: Calms liver inflammation, animal data
9. Fat metabolism: Modest weight loss
10. Appetite & satiety: Lower intake via GLP-1
11. Glucose & insulin (backed only by animal or user reports): Glucose control in animals
12. Neural protection (backed only by animal or user reports): Nerve protection in animals

## How it works
13. Glucagon arm burns fat inside the liver · Glucagon receptor, hepatocytes · role Organ function
   The glucagon arm activates glucagon receptors on liver cells, which shifts them toward burning fat and spending energy. Fat stored inside the liver is used up faster. In a short human trial, liver fat fell far more than body weight, which fits this liver-first action.
14. Directly calms scar-making liver cells, in animals · Hepatic stellate cell activation down · role Inflammatory signaling
   Hepatic stellate cells are the liver cells that switch on and lay down scar tissue when the liver is injured. Hanmi reports the drug directly holds back that activation. In animal models this meant less inflammation and fibrosis, but whether it reverses scarring in people awaits the Phase 2b biopsy results.
15. GLP-1 arm cuts appetite · GLP-1 receptor · role Appetite & satiety
   The GLP-1 arm activates GLP-1 receptors in the brain's appetite centres, so people feel less hungry and eat less. It also offsets glucagon's tendency to push blood sugar up. Weight loss in the human trial was modest, as the design is aimed at the liver more than the scale.
16. GIP arm aids insulin release and fat handling · GIP receptor · role Fat metabolism
   The GIP arm activates GIP receptors, which help the pancreas release insulin when glucose is high and influence how fat tissue stores fat. This rounds out the triple design alongside glucagon and GLP-1. Its separate contribution has not been isolated in human studies.
17. Fc fragment stretches action to a week · LAPSCOVERY Fc conjugation · role Organ function
   The peptide is chemically linked to a fragment of a human antibody, the Fc piece, using Hanmi's LAPSCOVERY platform. The larger size keeps it from being filtered out by the kidneys. That stretches its action to about a week, so it is given once weekly.
18. Mechanism overview: Efocipegtrutide is a single peptide that activates the glucagon, GIP and GLP-1 receptors, chemically linked to a human IgG Fc fragment (Hanmi's LAPSCOVERY platform) so it escapes kidney clearance and lasts about a week. Glucagon receptor signalling in hepatocytes raises fat oxidation and energy use in the liver, and Hanmi reports direct suppression of hepatic stellate cell activation, the cells that lay down scar tissue. GLP-1 receptor activity cuts appetite and offsets glucagon's glucose-raising effect, and GIP receptor activity aids insulin release and fat handling.

## Dosage (community reported unless tagged)
19. Typical: 2–6 mg (Phase 2b) · once weekly · cycle Trial length (Phase 1b/2a 12 weeks) · route Sub-Q (verified)
20. Half-life: ~62–257 hours (dose-dependent)
21. Dose note: Only trial doses exist. At ~0.08 mg/kg the top Phase 1b/2a dose is roughly 6–8 mg for most adults, matching the Phase 2b top dose (inferred).
22. Most people take: Phase 2b tested 2, 4 and 6 mg weekly Sub-Q; Phase 1b/2a used 0.01–0.08 mg/kg weekly. No community dose exists; no oral form.
23. Phase 2b: 2, 4 or 6 mg · 1× weekly · trial length not stated · Sub-Q · for biopsy-confirmed MASH with fibrosis [S1] (verified)
24. Phase 1b/2a: 0.01–0.08 mg/kg · 1× weekly · 12 wk · Sub-Q · for obese adults with fatty liver [S2] (verified)

## What people report
25. No community use or first-hand reports found; it is a large Fc-fusion biologic that is unlikely to be made by peptide labs.
26. Liked / worked: Liver fat down up to 81% at 12 weeks
27. Liked / worked: 2–5% weight loss in 12 weeks
28. Liked / worked: Less liver fibrosis in animals than semaglutide or tirzepatide
29. Liked / worked: No dose cut for futility in Phase 2b
30. What worked: Liver fat fell up to 81% (vs 6% placebo) at 12 weeks at the top Phase 1b/2a dose, with about 2–5% weight loss; animal models showed less liver inflammation and fibrosis where semaglutide and tirzepatide did little.
31. Went wrong / did not work: Nausea and diarrhea, dose-dependent
32. Went wrong / did not work: Two cases of high blood sugar
33. Went wrong / did not work: Modest weight loss
34. Went wrong / did not work: No Phase 2b results yet
35. What went wrong: Dose-dependent nausea and diarrhea; two subjects developed high blood sugar that resolved on stopping; weight loss is modest; no Phase 2b efficacy data published yet.
36. Most reported: No community reports found
37. Most reported: Not realistically made by peptide labs
38. Most reported: Watched as a liver-first triple agonist

## What has been tested
39. Organ function: Liver fat in obese NAFLD, Phase 1b/2a (human)
40. Inflammatory signaling: Liver inflammation and fibrosis models (animal)
41. Fat metabolism: Body weight, Phase 1b/2a (human)
42. Neural protection: Neuroprotection posters (animal)
43. Phase 1 and a 12-week Phase 1b/2a in obese adults with fatty liver, then a global Phase 2b in biopsy-confirmed MASH with fibrosis (US and Korea, 2, 4 and 6 mg weekly), completed July 2026.
44. What it helps: Human evidence so far is a 12-week Phase 1b/2a in obese adults with fatty liver, where liver fat fell up to 81% against 6% on placebo with 2–5% weight loss. Animal models showed less liver inflammation and fibrosis, which semaglutide and tirzepatide barely touched. The Phase 2b biopsy trial in MASH finished in July 2026 and is unreported. There is no meaningful community use.
45. Trial: active · Phase 2 · MASH liver disease · NCT04505436 · Hanmi Pharmaceutical. Hanmi's once monthly triple agonist Phase 2b liver trial is active, not recruiting, with completion estimated mid 2026. (checked 2026-10-23) [S3] (reported)

## Who shouldn't take it
46. Personal or family history of MTC or MEN2: Causes thyroid C-cell tumours in rodents; boxed warning and contraindication on the label. (inferred)
47. Anyone booked for surgery, endoscopy or sedation: Food can stay in the stomach for days and be inhaled into the lungs under anaesthesia. (inferred)
48. People with arrhythmia or a fast resting pulse: The glucagon part of the drug pushes resting heart rate up. (inferred)

## Where it comes from
49. Hanmi's weekly glucagon/GIP/GLP-1 triple agonist, bolted to an antibody Fc fragment with its LAPSCOVERY platform so it lasts days instead of minutes; built for liver fibrosis rather than maximum weight loss.
50. First studied for: MASH with liver fibrosis; orphan designations for primary sclerosing cholangitis, primary biliary cholangitis and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
51. Name story: Coded HM15211 and branded LAPS Triple Agonist. The name reads as ef- (the Fc prefix Hanmi also uses in efpeglenatide and efinopegdutide), -peg- (linker) and -trutide (triple agonist), though no official breakdown was found. [S4] (inferred)

# Lemon Bottle
Page: https://baresignals.co/library/#/p/lemon-bottle
Checked against Library v68, exported 2026-10-25

## Identity
1. Also called: Lemon Bottle fat dissolving, Lemon Bottle lipolysis solution, Lemon Bottle Fat Dissolve, 레몬보틀
2. Origin: Cosmetic solution: vitamin + enzyme + phospholipid
3. Legal and approval status: Switzerland: illegal unauthorised medicine (Swissmedic warning, 26 Mar 2024). Finland: Fimea and Tukes warning (28 Mar 2024); cosmetics may not be injected. UK: MHRA treats it as a cosmetic, not a medicine; the GPhC warned pharmacies off selling it (Apr 2025). US: not FDA-approved; FDA warned spas in 2010 that injectable fat dissolvers are unapproved. Korea: sold as a cosmetic; no regulator action found. Australia: no TGA statement found.

## Summary
4. Lemon Bottle is a Korean cosmetic solution sold as a fat dissolver and injected under the skin. Its label lists riboflavin, bromelain (a pineapple enzyme) and lecithin, and it is claimed to break down fat cells, though no data back this. No human or animal study exists, regulators say no effect is proven, and lab tests found mislabelled contents. Reports include swelling, lumps, infection and skin damage.
5. Punch line: Korean riboflavin, bromelain and lecithin mix, injected to melt spot fat. Its maker says not for injection.
6. Used for: Spot fat reduction: chin, belly, flanks, thighs

## Roles (what it is used for, strongest first)
7. Fat metabolism: Sold to dissolve spot fat
8. Skin & aesthetics: Used as a body-contouring cosmetic
9. Inflammatory signaling: Bromelain claimed to cut swelling
10. Cellular energy: Riboflavin is a fat-burning coenzyme, in theory

## How it works
11. Claimed to break fat cells down so they leave in urine · Maker's claim, no data · role Fat metabolism
   The maker says the product breaks down fat cells so their contents leave in urine. No study describes how it would do this, and the product contains no deoxycholic acid, the detergent that licensed fat dissolving injections use. Swissmedic found tested packs did not match their label.
12. Phospholipid similar to the 'PC' in older fat dissolvers · Lecithin / phosphatidylcholine · role Fat metabolism
   Lecithin supplies phosphatidylcholine, the phospholipid used in older off-label fat dissolving mixes. In those mixes the fat cell damage came mostly from the deoxycholate added to dissolve it, not from phosphatidylcholine itself. Lecithin alone is not an established fat cell destroying agent.
13. Pineapple enzyme claimed to reduce swelling · Bromelain, protease · role Inflammatory signaling
   Bromelain is a group of protein-cutting enzymes (proteases) from pineapple stem. It is marketed here to reduce swelling and downtime after injection. There is no study of injected bromelain in this product, so any anti-swelling effect is a claim, not a finding.
14. Vitamin that helps enzymes burn fat · Riboflavin → FAD, β-oxidation · role Cellular energy
   Riboflavin, vitamin B2, becomes FAD, a cofactor the enzymes of beta-oxidation need to burn fatty acids. Extra riboflavin corrects a deficiency but is not known to speed fat burning in people with normal levels. No study tests it as a fat loss injection.
15. Mechanism overview: Licensed injection lipolysis relies on deoxycholic acid, a bile-acid detergent that lyses adipocyte membranes and triggers an inflammatory clearance response. Older off-label 'lipodissolve' mixes combined phosphatidylcholine with deoxycholate as solubiliser. Lemon Bottle declares lecithin (a phosphatidylcholine source), bromelain (cysteine proteases from pineapple stem) and riboflavin (precursor of FAD and FMN, cofactors in fatty-acid beta-oxidation), and its maker states it contains no deoxycholic acid. None of these is an established adipocytolytic agent on its own, and no mechanism study exists for the product. Some clinic consent forms nonetheless list deoxycholic acid, and Swissmedic found declared ingredients absent or replaced in tested samples.

## What is inside the blend
16. Riboflavin (vitamin B2): null not disclosed · Coenzyme in fat burning; gives the yellow colour
17. Bromelain: null not disclosed · Pineapple enzyme, claimed to cut swelling
18. Lecithin: null not disclosed · Phospholipid, the 'PC' of older fat dissolvers

22. Version Some clinic consent forms: Deoxycholic acid · Riboflavin · Bromelain = Not disclosed
23. Why Lecithin is in it: The only part related to known injectable fat dissolvers
24. Why Bromelain is in it: Marketed to reduce swelling and downtime
25. Why Riboflavin is in it: Marketed to speed fat metabolism
26. Mixing chemistry: Sold as a ready solution labelled as a cosmetic, not made or tested to sterile injectable standards.
27. Mixing chemistry: Riboflavin breaks down in light; colour fading is a sign of exposure.
28. Mixing chemistry: Bromelain is a protein enzyme that loses activity in heat and can trigger allergy.
29. Mixing chemistry: Lab tests showed contents can differ from the label and between packs.

## Who shouldn't take it

## Synergies (paired with)
56. L-Carnitine: L-carnitine carries fatty acids into mitochondria to be burned, and oral trials show a small extra weight loss. Clinics pair it with Lemon Bottle to burn whatever fat is released. The pair has never been tested together.
57. Lipo-C: Lipo-C supplies liver fat export nutrients and carnitine, while Lemon Bottle is injected locally into a fat pocket. Clinics combine them as whole-body plus spot treatment. Neither has a fat loss trial, and the pair has not been tested.
58. MIC + B12: MIC + B12 gives lipotropes for liver fat export and B12, while Lemon Bottle targets one area. Clinics offer both in fat loss packages. Neither product has a weight loss trial, so the pairing is user logic, not trial data.
59. AOD-9604: AOD-9604, a growth hormone fragment, was shown to block new fat storage in rodents. Users add it to Lemon Bottle for spot fat work. The pairing is user logic, not trial data.
60. HGH frag 176–191: HGH frag 176–191 raised fat breakdown in obese mice and is often injected locally, the same way Lemon Bottle is used. People pair them for stubborn areas. The pair has not been tested together.
61. Adipotide: Adipotide cuts the blood supply to white fat and shrank fat in obese monkeys, but injured kidneys at higher doses. It is a far stronger and riskier agent than Lemon Bottle. The pairing has no data at all.

## Where it comes from
62. A Korean 'fat-dissolving' solution sold as a cosmetic and injected under the skin in salons and clinics. The maker lists riboflavin (vitamin B2), bromelain (a pineapple enzyme) and lecithin (a phospholipid) as its core ingredients, and says it contains no deoxycholic acid.
63. First studied for: Went viral on TikTok in 2023 (over 80 million views by year end) as a cheap, 'no downtime' fat dissolver for chins, bellies and thighs.
64. Name story: A brand name: 'Lemon' for the fresh, natural image and the yellow riboflavin colour, 'Bottle' for the vial. It contains no lemon as a declared active. [S1] (inferred)
65. 2010: FDA warns US spas: injectable fat dissolvers are unapproved
66. 2015: Deoxycholic acid approved in the US for double chin, the licensed alternative
67. 2023: Lemon Bottle goes viral on TikTok; UK complaints jump to 90
68. Mar 2024: Swissmedic declares it illegal; lab finds mislabelled contents. Finland warns too
69. Apr 2025: UK pharmacy regulator warns pharmacies off selling it
70. Today: Still sold as a cosmetic and injected in salons

# Cartalax + Tβ4 + BPC-157
Page: https://baresignals.co/library/#/p/cartalax-tb4-bpc
Checked against Library v68, exported 2026-10-25

## Identity
1. Also called: Cartalax/TB4/BPC 20 mg, AED + thymosin beta-4 + BPC-157, joint blend, cartilage blend
2. Origin: Blend of 3 peptides
3. Legal and approval status: US: not approved. BPC-157 and the TB-500 fragment were removed from FDA Category 2 on 15 Apr 2026 and won an 8-6-1 PCAC vote in July 2026; full Tβ4 and Cartalax were not on that list. WADA: Tβ4 and BPC-157 banned. Russia: AED sold as an oral bioregulator supplement, not a medicine.

## Summary
4. This three-peptide joint blend combines the cartilage bioregulator Cartalax with full thymosin beta-4 and BPC-157. People combine them so Cartalax targets cartilage cells while the other two bring blood supply and general tissue repair. Evidence is per component, Cartalax data is cell culture and Russian sources, and no study has tested the three together.
5. Punch line: Cartalax targets cartilage; Tβ4 and BPC-157 add blood flow and repair. Used for knee and hip wear.
6. Used for: Joint and cartilage support

## Roles (what it is used for, strongest first)
7. Bone & cartilage: Cartalax aimed at cartilage cells
8. Tissue repair: Tβ4 and BPC-157 tissue repair
9. Inflammatory signaling: All three dampen inflammation
10. Aging & senescence: Bioregulator framed as anti-aging for joints
11. Muscle & performance (backed only by animal or user reports): Tβ4 and BPC-157 used for muscle injury

## How it works
12. Prompts cartilage cells to multiply, in culture · AED on chondrocyte proliferation · role Bone & cartilage
   Cartalax, the tripeptide AED, acts on chondrocytes, the cells that make and maintain cartilage. In rat chondrocyte cultures it raised cell numbers, more so in cells from old rats. This is cell data only, from the Khavinson bioregulator line.
13. Said to switch on cartilage matrix genes · Collagen II, aggrecan (claimed) · role Bone & cartilage
   AED is claimed to switch on cartilage matrix genes, mainly collagen type II and aggrecan, the proteins that give cartilage its strength and cushion. That would rebuild matrix rather than only add cells. This rests on Russian bioregulator claims, not independent data.
14. Moves repair cells and builds new vessels · G-actin sequestering, cell migration · role Tissue repair
   Thymosin beta-4 binds G-actin so repair cells can move, and it promotes new blood vessels. Joint tissue has a poor blood supply, so bringing in cells and vessels is the logic for its role here. It has Phase 2 human trials in wounds and dry eye, but not in joints.
15. Speeds tendon and ligament healing in animals · Angiogenesis, FAK-paxillin · role Tissue repair
   BPC-157 drives vessel growth and moves tendon fibroblasts through the FAK-paxillin pathway. That speeds tendon and ligament healing around the joint in rodent models. Human data are thin, and no study tests the three together.
16. Mechanism overview: Cartalax is the tripeptide Ala-Glu-Asp (AED), from the Khavinson bioregulator line, claimed to act on chondrocyte gene expression; published data are rat chondrocyte cultures showing more cell division. Thymosin beta-4 is a 43-residue actin-sequestering peptide that promotes cell migration and angiogenesis, with phase 2 human wound and eye trials. BPC-157 is a 15-residue gastric fragment that speeds tendon and ligament healing in rodents. The stack pairs a cartilage-specific signal with two general repair signals.

## What is inside the blend
17. Cartalax (AED): 10 mg · Cartilage cell signal
18. Tβ4: 5 mg · Cell migration and new blood vessels
19. BPC-157: 5 mg · Tendon and ligament healing
20. Most common ratio: Cartalax 10 · TB-500 5 · BPC-157 5 = 20 mg (6 of 13 listings (tied))
21. Other ratio seen: Cartalax 10 · TB-500 10 · BPC-157 10 = 30 mg (6 listings (tied))
22. Other ratio seen: Cartalax 20 · TB-500 5 · BPC-157 5 (page contradicts itself) = 30 mg (1 listing)
23. Version Common retail: Cartalax 10 · Tβ4 5 · BPC-157 5 = 20 mg
24. Why Cartalax is in it: The only part aimed at cartilage cells themselves
25. Why Tβ4 is in it: Moves repair cells and builds vessels into poorly supplied joint tissue
26. Why BPC-157 is in it: Tendon and ligament repair around the joint
27. Mixing chemistry: Tβ4 is most stable around pH 5.5 to 6, BPC-157 around 6.5 to 8.5 by their patents; the vial is a compromise.
28. Mixing chemistry: Tβ4 carries a methionine that oxidises (its main breakdown product); keep the vial cold and away from light.
29. Mixing chemistry: Cartalax is half the vial's mass and is an acidic tripeptide (two acid residues), so it likely sets the vial's pH.
30. Mixing chemistry: At 43 residues Tβ4 is the one most likely to clump; gentle swirling, no shaking.
31. Self-mixing: Separate vials let you dose Tβ4 and BPC-157 at their usual amounts instead of the low share they get here, at the cost of more injections or an unknown combined pH.

## Dosage (community reported unless tagged)
32. Typical: No standard dose · 1× daily · cycle 30 days to 8 weeks · route Sub-Q (reported)
33. Half-life: per component
34. Most people take: No published blend dose. People size it on Cartalax (about 1 mg a day in stack posts). 20 mg in 2 mL: 10 units gives 500 mcg Cartalax, 250 mcg Tβ4, 250 mcg BPC-157; 20 units doubles it.

## What people report
35. Sub-Q once daily, usually 30 days to 8 weeks. One promoter's joint stack runs Cartalax 1 mg, BPC-157 500 mcg and TB-500 500 mcg daily (plus GHK-Cu); this blend can't reach that BPC dose without overshooting Cartalax.
36. Liked / worked: Each part has a distinct joint role
37. Liked / worked: Tβ4 has human phase 2 wound data
38. Liked / worked: AED raised chondrocyte numbers in culture
39. What worked: No blend-specific report pool. Writers promoting Cartalax stacks say people whose joints improved on BPC-157 and TB-500 but never felt restored describe joints that finally felt different with Cartalax added. Unquantified.
40. Went wrong / did not work: Cartalax evidence is preclinical
41. Went wrong / did not work: Tβ4 and BPC-157 underdosed at this ratio
42. Went wrong / did not work: No trial of the stack
43. What went wrong: All Cartalax joint claims are preclinical or from Russian bioregulator sources. At this ratio Tβ4 and BPC-157 are dosed well below their usual standalone amounts. Cartilage change takes months, so short runs are easy to misread. No adverse-event data for the combination.
44. Most reported: Run 30 days to 8 weeks
45. Most reported: Picked for knees and hips, early wear
46. Most reported: Promoters say it helps after BPC/TB plateaus

## What has been tested
47. Never tested as a combination. Cartalax (AED) has rat chondrocyte cultures (cell numbers up 1.4 to 2.1 times, more in cells from old rats) and Russian bioregulator literature; Tβ4 has phase 2 human wound and eye trials; BPC-157 has animal injury models. A June 2026 stack review calls the joint stack community practice, not validated practice.
48. What it helps: Evidence is per component. AED: cell culture only. Tβ4: phase 2 human trials in pressure ulcers, epidermolysis bullosa and dry eye. BPC-157: rodent injury models, thin human data. No study tests them together; joint benefit is promoter-reported and unquantified.

## Who shouldn't take it
49. People with active or recent cancer: Raises VEGFR2 signalling and new vessel growth in animal work; tumours use the same pathway. (inferred)
50. Drug-tested athletes: Banned since 2022 under S0 (non-approved substances); positives have led to bans. (verified)
51. People treating a diagnosed joint disease with it: No controlled trials show benefit; delays proven care. (inferred)
52. People with proliferative retinopathy or vascular malformations: Pro-angiogenic peptides could feed abnormal vessel growth. (inferred)

## Synergies (paired with)
53. GHK-Cu: GHK-Cu adds copper delivery and collagen remodelling, while the stack aims at cartilage cells and joint repair. People add it for broader matrix support. Nothing here has been tested together, so the pairing is user logic, not trial data.
54. KPV: KPV blocks NF-κB in immune cells, while the stack works on cartilage and soft tissue repair. People add it to calm inflamed joints during repair. The combination has not been tested.
55. Chonluten: Chonluten is another Khavinson bioregulator, claimed to tune airway tissue genes, while Cartalax is the cartilage member of the same line. People run several bioregulators in one course. Both rest on claimed data, and the pair has not been tested together.

## Where it comes from
56. A three-peptide joint vial: the cartilage bioregulator Cartalax (Ala-Glu-Asp, 10 mg) with full thymosin beta-4 (5 mg) and BPC-157 (5 mg).
57. First studied for: Built for joints: Cartalax aimed at cartilage cells, Tβ4 and BPC-157 for general tissue repair and blood supply.
58. Name story: Cart from cartilage plus the -lax ending used across the Khavinson bioregulator range. The active is the tripeptide Ala-Glu-Asp, AED. [S1] (inferred)
59. 1981: Thymosin beta-4 sequenced
60. 1993: BPC-157 first published

# Insulin
Page: https://baresignals.co/library/#/p/insulin
Checked against Library v68, exported 2026-10-25

## Identity
1. Also called: proinsulin hormone, human insulin, regular insulin, isletin (historic)
2. Origin: Made by the body
3. Sequence: FVNQHLCGSHLVEALYLVCGERGFFYTPKTRREAEDLQVGQVELGGGPGAGSLQPLALEGSLQKRGIVEQCCTSICSLYQLENYCN (86 amino acids). Shown as proinsulin, the single chain the body first makes. Two cuts remove the middle; the B chain (first 30) and A chain (last 21) stay, joined by two bridges between C pairs
4. Legal and approval status: Approved worldwide. A reference molecule in this encyclopedia.

## Summary
5. Insulin is a hormone made by the body that controls blood sugar. It moves glucose from the blood into cells, stops the liver releasing more, and tells the body to store fat. It is the life-saving treatment for type 1 diabetes, but misuse for muscle building can cause fatal hypoglycemia.
6. Punch line: The body's master storage hormone: pulls sugar into cells and signals fat storage. Life-saving in type 1 diabetes.
7. Used for: Blood sugar control in diabetes

## Roles (what it is used for, strongest first)
8. Glucose & insulin: Moves sugar out of the blood into cells
9. Cellular energy: Lets cells take in fuel
10. Fat metabolism: Tells the body to store fat

## How it works
11. Pulls glucose into muscle and fat · Insulin receptor, GLUT4 · role Glucose & insulin
   Insulin binds the insulin receptor, a tyrosine kinase, which switches on the PI3K and Akt chain inside the cell. Akt sends GLUT4 glucose transporters to the surface of muscle and fat cells, so sugar moves out of the blood and into tissue. This is textbook physiology, confirmed by a century of human use.
12. Stops the liver releasing glucose · Hepatic insulin signalling · role Glucose & insulin
   In the liver, the same insulin signal shuts down the making and release of new glucose. Between meals the liver is the main source of blood sugar, so turning it off is a large part of how insulin lowers glucose. In type 1 diabetes, losing this brake is why sugar runs high even when fasting.
13. Stores fat, blocks fat breakdown · Lipogenesis, lipolysis block · role Fat metabolism
   In fat tissue, insulin blocks hormone-sensitive lipase, the enzyme that frees stored fat, and pushes cells to build and store fat instead. The body shifts from burning its reserves to filling them. This is why steady high insulin favours fat storage, a well-established effect in human physiology.
14. Fills muscle and liver glycogen stores · Glycogen synthase · role Cellular energy
   Insulin activates glycogen synthase, the enzyme that links glucose into glycogen, the stored form of sugar in muscle and liver. Those stores fill after meals and are drawn on during exercise and fasting. Misusing insulin to drive this refill for muscle building risks hypoglycemia, which can be fatal.
15. Mechanism overview: Insulin binds the insulin receptor, a tyrosine kinase on muscle, fat and liver cells. The receptor phosphorylates IRS proteins, which switch on PI3K and Akt. In muscle and fat, Akt moves GLUT4 transporters to the cell surface, so glucose floods in. In the liver, the same signal shuts down glucose output and activates glycogen synthase to store sugar. In fat tissue it blocks hormone-sensitive lipase and drives fat storage. The net result: blood glucose falls fast, and the body shifts from burning stores to filling them.

## Dosage (community reported unless tagged)
16. Typical: 0.4–1 U/kg/day · basal plus meals · cycle ongoing · route Sub-Q, IV (verified)
17. Half-life: ~5 min IV

## What people report
18. Listed here as a reference hormone, not a Bare Signals product.
19. Liked / worked: Life-saving in type 1 diabetes
20. Liked / worked: A century of refined analogues
21. What worked: Life-saving, foundational diabetes therapy.
22. Went wrong / did not work: Hypoglycemia is the central danger
23. Went wrong / did not work: Muscle-building misuse can be fatal
24. What went wrong: Hypoglycemia is the central danger; misuse for muscle-building is dangerous and sometimes fatal.
25. Most reported: Reference hormone, not a product

## What has been tested
26. Glucose & insulin: Type 1 diabetes (human)
27. Glucose & insulin: Type 2 diabetes (human)
28. Glucose & insulin: Many long and fast analogues (human)
29. A century of clinical use and refinement across many analogues.
30. What it helps: Insulin is the life-saving treatment for type 1 diabetes, where the body makes none, and a mainstay in advanced type 2 diabetes. A century of refined fast and long analogues lets people match both meals and baseline needs. It sits in this library as a reference hormone. Misuse for muscle building shows its edge: hypoglycemia can be fatal.
31. Trial: active · Phase 1 · intranasal insulin after spinal cord injury · NCT07384052 · HealthPartners Institute. Approved since the 1920s and still in constant trials; one recruiting study tests an insulin nasal spray in spinal cord injury. (checked 2026-10-23) [S1] (reported)

## Who shouldn't take it
32. People on beta-blockers: Can hide warning signs of low blood sugar. (verified)
33. People with low potassium: Insulin drives potassium into cells; arrhythmia risk. (verified)
34. People taking pioglitazone: Fluid retention and heart failure with insulin. (verified)
35. People with hypoglycemia unawareness: Without shakes or sweating as a warning, a low can progress to collapse. (verified)

## Where it comes from
36. The first protein ever sequenced (1955) and the first hormone injected to save a life (1922); in 1982 the first medicine made by engineered bacteria.
37. First studied for: Type 1 diabetes, and later type 2.
38. Name story: From Latin insula, island, for the pancreatic islets that make it. Belgian Jean de Meyer coined the word in 1909, over a decade before Banting's team isolated the hormone, which they briefly called "isletin". [S2] (verified)
39. 1922: First hormone injected to save a life
40. 1955: First protein ever sequenced
41. 1982: First medicine made by engineered bacteria
42. Today: Foundational diabetes therapy; a reference hormone here

## Sources
